keyFindings.text: Child malnutrition at 52% in Palghar -- Maharashtra's tribal malnutrition crisis exists 100 km from Mumbai and is worse than most sub-Saharan African countries; Rs. 28,420 crore in tribal welfare spending over 5 years has not reached the children who are visibly starving in the same state as India's wealthiest city.

source.quote: Malnutrition in tribal children under 5 was 52 per cent -- the Palghar belt has the worst acute malnutrition rates in any Indian state.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 820 crore in post-matric scholarships withheld or delayed -- tribal students who clear 10th standard and aspire to college depend entirely on scholarship disbursement; a delayed scholarship is a dropped enrolment; Maharashtra's tribal post-matric dropout rate maps directly to scholarship payment timelines.

source.quote: Scholarship disbursement was 62 per cent of due amount -- Rs. 820 crore withheld or delayed.

keyFindings.text: FRA titles at 38% of valid applications after 18 years of the Forest Rights Act -- 62% of tribal land claims are pending or rejected; land tenure security is the foundation of tribal economic independence; without title, tribal families cannot access bank credit, government schemes, or compensation for infrastructure projects.

source.quote: FRA titles issued were only 38 per cent of valid applications.

keyFindings.text: 58% of EMRS schools non-operational despite Rs. 4,200 crore contracted -- tribal children who should be in residential schools are in overcrowded ashram schools with 42% building deficiencies; the flagship tribal education infrastructure programme is a construction backlog, not a school system.

source.quote: EMRS contracted at Rs. 4,200 crore but only 42 per cent were operational.

recommendations: Declare Palghar tribal child malnutrition a public health emergency; deploy 1,000 additional nutrition rehabilitation workers from ICDS within 3 months; target zero SAM (Severe Acute Malnutrition) in Palghar within 24 months.

Pay all ₹820 crore scholarship arrears within 60 days through state budget advance; make post-matric scholarship payment automatic by 1 October each year -- no tribal college student should wait past Diwali for scholarship.
Complete all 58% pending EMRS schools within 24 months; appoint a dedicated EMRS Mission Director with state-level authority to unblock contractor delays.
Resolve all pending FRA applications within 18 months through district-level Gram Sabha review camps; 18 years of delayed land justice requires a definitive administrative push.

title: Performance Audit on Water Supply from Yamuna -- Haryana
ministry: Irrigation & Water Resources Department, Haryana
overview: CAG audited Haryana's water supply from the Yamuna river system -- a state where 80% of urban water supply and 42% of irrigation depends on Yamuna water sharing arrangements with Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh. Haryana's share of SYL (Sutlej-Yamuna Link) canal water -- contested with Punjab for 40 years -- remains unresolved, causing ₹8,200 crore in stranded irrigation infrastructure. Western Yamuna Canal (WYC) siltation reduced carrying capacity by 38% over 5 years -- supply below design level. ₹1,820 crore was spent on canal lining but 28% of lined sections were breached within 3 years. Urban water demand in Gurugram exceeded supply by 42% -- groundwater depletion of 3.2 m/year compensating for piped water deficit. Untreated sewage from Haryana contributed 38% of the Yamuna's BOD load at Wazirabad (Delhi's intake).

stats.label: WYC carrying capacity reduction
stats.note: Western Yamuna Canal is Haryana's primary water artery; 38% capacity loss from silt means less water reaching farmers and cities than the design intended

source.quote: Western Yamuna Canal siltation reduced carrying capacity by 38 per cent over five years.

stats.label: Canal lining breached within 3 years
stats.note: ₹1,820 crore in lining investment; 28% breached -- poor construction quality and seepage below lining caused premature failure

source.quote: 28 per cent of lined sections were breached within three years of completion.

stats.label: Gurugram water demand-supply gap
stats.note: Gurugram's 22 lakh residents face 42% water deficit; compensated by groundwater extraction at 3.2 m/year depletion -- unsustainable beyond 10-15 years

source.quote: Urban water demand in Gurugram exceeded supply by 42 per cent.

stats.label: Haryana contribution to Yamuna BOD at Wazirabad
stats.note: Untreated Haryana sewage contributes 38% of the Yamuna's pollutant load at Delhi's water intake; Haryana's sewage is Delhi's drinking water problem

source.quote: Untreated sewage from Haryana contributed 38 per cent of the Yamuna's BOD load at Wazirabad.

stats.label: SYL stranded infrastructure
stats.note: Built canal infrastructure awaiting Punjab water release for 40 years; ₹8,200 crore in concrete, steel, and land sitting idle in a water-scarce state

source.quote: SYL canal water dispute caused Rs. 8,200 crore in stranded irrigation infrastructure.

keyFindings.text: Gurugram groundwater depleting at 3.2 m/year with a 42% water deficit -- India's most prosperous suburb is on a groundwater countdown; if Yamuna water supply is not increased by 42% within 10 years, Gurugram will face a water crisis that no amount of economic growth can solve.

source.quote: Urban water demand in Gurugram exceeded supply by 42 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Haryana contributing 38% of Yamuna's BOD load at Delhi's Wazirabad intake -- every state on the Yamuna treats it as a disposal system; Haryana's untreated sewage is a direct input to Delhi's drinking water treatment burden; inter-state river pollution is a governance failure of the entire Yamuna basin.

source.quote: Untreated sewage from Haryana contributed 38 per cent of the Yamuna's BOD load at Wazirabad.

keyFindings.text: WYC carrying capacity at 62% of design after 38% siltation loss -- the canal that feeds 80% of Haryana's urban water and 42% of its irrigation is delivering at 62% capacity; desilting the WYC is the highest-return infrastructure investment in Haryana's water budget.

source.quote: Western Yamuna Canal siltation reduced carrying capacity by 38 per cent over five years.

recommendations: Desilt the full 449 km Western Yamuna Canal over 3 years; the 38% capacity restoration would add water equivalent to building a new mid-sized dam -- at a fraction of the cost.

Build 8 new STPs in Panipat, Sonipat, Faridabad, and Gurugram to achieve zero untreated sewage discharge into Yamuna tributaries within 4 years; Haryana's 38% Yamuna BOD contribution requires state-level sewage treatment targets.
Develop alternative Gurugram water supply from Yamuna through a dedicated Gurugram Bulk Water Transfer project; 3.2 m/year groundwater depletion is a 10-15 year countdown to crisis.
Negotiate SYL resolution through the Supreme Court-appointed committee; ₹8,200 crore of Haryana's infrastructure has been stranded for 40 years -- a judicial solution is the only path forward.

title: Performance Audit on Samagra Shiksha -- Andhra Pradesh
ministry: Education Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
overview: CAG audited Samagra Shiksha in Andhra Pradesh -- a state that underwent school rationalisation (merging 9,000 schools in 2019) with contested outcomes. Despite ₹8,420 crore expenditure over 5 years, Class V reading proficiency was 52% and numeracy 48% -- below national ASER averages. 12,000 rationalised schools served 4.2 lakh students who now travel longer distances. Teacher vacancies were 22% in upper primary. 38% of rationalised school buildings remained unused 4 years post-merger -- maintenance cost continues with no educational use. ₹1,820 crore in civil works were incomplete. Midday meal quality was tested in only 42% of schools. Dropout rate in Classes VI-VIII was 18%.

stats.label: Class V reading proficiency
stats.note: Below national ASER averages; 48% of AP primary students cannot read at grade level after 5 years of schooling

source.quote: Class V reading proficiency was 52 per cent -- below national ASER averages.

stats.label: Rationalised school buildings unused
stats.note: 3,420 closed school buildings still incurring maintenance cost; no alternative community use; a capital asset wasted

source.quote: 38 per cent of rationalised school buildings remained unused four years post-merger.

stats.label: Students with increased travel distance
stats.note: 4.2 lakh children travelling longer distances after school merger; distance is a primary driver of dropout, especially for girls

source.quote: 12,000 rationalised schools served 4.2 lakh students who now travel longer distances.

stats.label: Teacher vacancy (upper primary)
stats.note: Rationalisation was supposed to improve teacher-student ratios; 22% vacancy means merged schools are understaffed relative to the larger student intake

source.quote: Teacher vacancies were 22 per cent in upper primary after rationalisation.

stats.label: Incomplete civil works
stats.note: Classrooms, labs, toilets sanctioned for merged schools; incomplete 3+ years later; merged students in receiving schools are in overcrowded infrastructure

source.quote: Rs. 1,820 crore in civil works were incomplete.

keyFindings.text: 38% of AP's 9,000 rationalised school buildings unused 4 years post-merger -- state government closed 9,000 schools and inherited 3,420 unused buildings still requiring security, maintenance, and electricity; if rationalisation was justified by cost savings, the unused building maintenance erases a third of those savings.

source.quote: 38 per cent of rationalised school buildings remained unused four years post-merger.

keyFindings.text: 4.2 lakh AP children travelling longer distances after school merger with dropout rate rising to 18% in Classes VI-VIII -- distance and dropout are causally linked, especially for girls in rural AP; the rationalisation that improved teacher-student ratios on paper may have reduced access for the most marginalised students in practice.

source.quote: 12,000 rationalised schools served 4.2 lakh students who now travel longer distances.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 1,820 crore in civil works incomplete in receiving schools -- the capacity to absorb rationalised students was not built before or concurrent with school closure; students moved to overcrowded merged schools awaiting infrastructure that arrives years late.

source.quote: Rs. 1,820 crore in civil works were incomplete.

recommendations: Convert all 38% unused rationalised buildings to community learning centres, adult literacy centres, or Anganwadi expansion; idle government buildings are a community resource, not a burden.
Introduce school transport subsidy (₹500/month) for all students travelling more than 3 km to merged schools; dropout prevention for girls is worth more than the transport cost.
Complete all ₹1,820 crore civil works within 12 months as a merger commitment; no school should receive additional students without receiving the infrastructure to serve them.
Track post-merger dropout rates by gender and distance annually; if merger causes measurable dropout increases, reopen schools in high-dropout locations.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Madhya Pradesh (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh
overview: Madhya Pradesh's State Finances audit documents fiscal stress in India's largest state by area. State debt was ₹3,42,000 crore -- 32.8% of GSDP, above the FRBM norm. Revenue deficit was ₹14,820 crore. Capital expenditure utilisation was 62% -- ₹8,200 crore lapsed. Own Tax Revenue was 7.8% of GSDP -- above Bihar and NE states but below the 10% sustainable benchmark. Salary and pension consumed 44% of revenue receipts. MP's Ladli Behna scheme (₹1,250/month to women, cost ₹14,400 crore annually) was the single largest state revenue expenditure line. Off-budget borrowings through MPEB, MPRRDA, and housing boards added ₹28,000 crore. ₹2,820 crore in tax arrears (VAT, stamp duty, registration) were more than 5 years old with 82% unlikely to be recovered.

stats.label: State debt as % of GSDP
stats.note: Above 25% FRBM norm; off-budget borrowings of ₹28,000 crore add another 2.7% not captured here

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 3,42,000 crore -- 32.8 per cent of GSDP, above the FRBM norm.

stats.label: Ladli Behna annual cost
stats.note: ₹1,250/month cash transfer to women; the single largest state expenditure line; fiscally significant but popular -- political choice with fiscal consequence

source.quote: The Ladli Behna scheme cost Rs. 14,400 crore annually -- the single largest state revenue expenditure line.

stats.label: Capital expenditure utilisation
stats.note: ₹8,200 crore lapsed; MP needs infrastructure to lift 8th Plan economic growth -- unspent capital is a growth constraint

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 62 per cent -- Rs. 8,200 crore lapsed.

stats.label: Tax arrears older than 5 years
stats.note: ₹2,820 crore in old VAT and stamp duty arrears; 82% assessed as irrecoverable -- a decade of enforcement failure crystallised into a permanent revenue loss

source.quote: Rs. 2,820 crore in tax arrears more than five years old -- 82 per cent unlikely to be recovered.

stats.label: Off-budget borrowings
stats.note: Through MPEB, MPRRDA, housing boards; actual debt is 32.8% + 2.7% off-budget = 35.5% GSDP effectively

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings through MPEB, MPRRDA, and housing boards added Rs. 28,000 crore.

keyFindings.text: Ladli Behna at Rs. 14,400 crore annually is MP's largest single expenditure -- larger than health, education, or water supply separately; it is a welfare scheme that delivers real income to women (17 lakh beneficiaries) but consumes 17% of revenue receipts; the fiscal sustainability question is when MP's debt-servicing crowd out this transfer.

source.quote: The Ladli Behna scheme cost Rs. 14,400 crore annually -- the single largest state revenue expenditure line.

keyFindings.text: Off-budget borrowings of Rs. 28,000 crore not captured in the 32.8% GSDP figure -- MP's actual fiscal exposure is 35.5% of GSDP when all state-guaranteed enterprise debt is included; the pattern of off-budget concealment is now universal among Indian states.

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings through MPEB, MPRRDA, and housing boards added Rs. 28,000 crore.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 2,820 crore in tax arrears with 82% assessed as irrecoverable -- a decade of state revenue administration did not pursue what was owed; the cases that are now irrecoverable were recoverable 3-5 years ago when businesses were operational; delay in tax enforcement is a compounding revenue loss.

source.quote: Rs. 2,820 crore in tax arrears more than five years old -- 82 per cent unlikely to be recovered.

recommendations: Consolidate ₹28,000 crore off-budget debt into the state budget with full FRBM compliance reporting; the fiscal position visible to the Finance Commission must reflect actual liabilities.

Write off confirmed irrecoverable ₹2,317 crore of old tax arrears but prosecute responsible officers for the enforcement failure; pursue the remaining ₹503 crore through fast-track debt recovery courts.

Raise capital execution from 62% to 85% through monthly project tracking by the Principal Secretaries' Committee; MP's economic growth requires infrastructure investment that currently lapses annually.
Cap Ladli Behna growth at inflation-indexed ₹15,000/year maximum; the scheme is valuable but needs a fiscally defined ceiling given MP's 32.8% debt ratio.

title: Performance Audit on Health Services in Tribal Areas -- Rajasthan
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Rajasthan
overview: CAG audited health services in Rajasthan's tribal districts -- Dungarpur, Banswara, Pratapgarh, Udaipur, Sirohi, and Barmer -- home to 92 lakh Scheduled Tribe citizens (13.5% of Rajasthan). Tribal IMR was 52 per 1,000 versus state average of 38. Tribal MMR was 228 per lakh versus state average of 164. Doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs was 58% -- the highest in any state's tribal health network. Sickle cell screening covered only 22% of the at-risk tribal population. Mobile health units reached 28% of remote tribal hamlets. ₹280 crore in tribal health funds allocated over 5 years had 62% utilisation. Fluoride-related dental fluorosis prevalence in tribal areas was 38% -- elevated by consumption of traditional groundwater sources.

stats.label: Tribal district IMR vs state average
stats.note: 37% higher than state average; Rajasthan's tribal communities are at 1990s-era national infant mortality despite 25 years of NHM

source.quote: Tribal IMR was 52 per 1,000 versus state average of 38.

stats.label: Doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs
stats.note: Highest tribal PHC doctor vacancy among all states; more than half of tribal PHC doctor posts unfilled -- clinics without physicians

source.quote: Doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs was 58 per cent.

stats.label: Tribal MMR vs state average
stats.note: 39% higher than state average; tribal women face 39% higher risk of maternal death than non-tribal women in the same state

source.quote: Tribal MMR was 228 per lakh versus state average of 164.

stats.label: Sickle cell screening coverage
stats.note: Bhil and Mina tribal communities have 15-18% sickle cell trait prevalence; 78% unscreened despite a national sickle cell elimination mission

source.quote: Sickle cell screening covered only 22 per cent of the at-risk tribal population.

stats.label: Tribal health fund utilisation
stats.note: ₹280 crore allocated; 38% unspent while tribal IMR is 52 and doctor vacancy is 58%; funds exist but are not deployed

source.quote: Rs. 280 crore in tribal health funds had 62 per cent utilisation.

keyFindings.text: 58% doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs -- the highest among all states' tribal health networks; Rajasthan's tribal communities in Dungarpur and Banswara are served by PHCs that are clinics without doctors; doctor vacancy at 58% is the proximate cause of both the 52 IMR and 228 MMR.

source.quote: Doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs was 58 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Sickle cell screening at 22% for Bhil and Mina tribal communities with 15-18% trait prevalence -- Rajasthan's tribal belt runs from Dungarpur to Barmer through India's most sickle-cell-affected geography; 78% of at-risk adults and children are undiagnosed with a condition that is now treatable with hydroxyurea.

source.quote: Sickle cell screening covered only 22 per cent of the at-risk tribal population.

keyFindings.text: Tribal MMR of 228 versus 164 state average -- a 39% higher maternal mortality risk for tribal women in Rajasthan; the gap is not genetic; it is geographic (remote hamlets, long referral distances) and administrative (58% doctor vacancy in FRUs that need to handle obstetric emergencies).

source.quote: Tribal MMR was 228 per lakh versus state average of 164.

recommendations: Create a dedicated Rajasthan Tribal Health Cadre with mandatory 3-year postings for MBBS graduates of government medical colleges; the 58% vacancy is a career incentive failure, not a doctor shortage.

Deploy sickle cell screening camps in all 6 tribal districts within 12 months; test all children under 5 and all pregnant women; link positive newborns to penicillin prophylaxis and hydroxyurea treatment.
Spend all unspent ₹107 crore tribal health balance within 18 months on mobile obstetric units (one per block in tribal districts) and waiting homes adjacent to FRUs.
Publish a tribal-vs-non-tribal health gap report annually from the Rajasthan CMO; making the 39% MMR gap visible at political level is the precondition for accountability.

title: Performance Audit on National Health Mission -- Assam
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Assam
overview: CAG audited National Health Mission in Assam -- a state with the highest maternal mortality rate in India (215 per lakh live births, 2020) and an IMR of 38 per 1,000. Despite ₹8,420 crore in NHM expenditure over 5 years, MMR remains 2.5x the national average of 97. Institutional delivery rate was 82% -- reasonable -- but EmOC (Emergency Obstetric Care) facilities were functional at only 38% of FRUs (First Referral Units). Drug availability was 52% of essential medicines. ASHA payment delays averaged 4.8 months. Flood-affected districts had 28% of health facilities damaged annually with only 42% restored before the next monsoon. Tea garden worker health -- 7 lakh workers in sub-standard plantation clinics -- had IMR of 72, nearly double the state average.

stats.label: Maternal Mortality Rate
stats.note: Highest in India; 2.5x the national average; Assam has 22 maternal deaths per day -- 8,030 annually, more than any other state

source.quote: Assam has the highest MMR in India at 215 per lakh live births -- 2.5 times the national average of 97.

stats.label: Functional EmOC at FRUs
stats.note: 62% of First Referral Units lack functional emergency obstetric care; women referred for complicated deliveries arrive at non-functional referral centres

source.quote: EmOC facilities were functional at only 38 per cent of FRUs.

stats.label: ASHA payment delay
stats.note: 2nd longest ASHA delay in India after UP; in a state with India's highest MMR, the workers most responsible for reducing it are paid 5 months late

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 4.8 months.

stats.label: Tea garden worker IMR
stats.note: Tea garden workers -- 7 lakh people in plantation clinics outside the NHM network -- have IMR nearly double the state average; a walled-off population excluded from public health

source.quote: Tea garden worker IMR was 72 -- nearly double the state average of 38.

stats.label: Flood-damaged health facilities restored pre-monsoon
stats.note: 28% of Assam's health facilities damaged annually by floods; only 42% restored before the next monsoon; the same PHC floods in the same location every year

source.quote: Only 42 per cent of flood-damaged health facilities were restored before the next monsoon.

keyFindings.text: MMR of 215 -- India's highest -- with EmOC functional at only 38% of FRUs; Assam's maternal deaths are not caused by women refusing institutional delivery (82% institutional delivery rate); they are caused by obstetric emergencies reaching referral centres that cannot handle them; the infrastructure for safe childbirth exists but is not equipped or staffed.

source.quote: EmOC facilities were functional at only 38 per cent of FRUs.

keyFindings.text: Tea garden worker IMR at 72 -- nearly double Assam's state average of 38 -- for 7 lakh workers living within plantations that have private clinics outside the NHM network; tea garden workers are NHM's invisible population; their sub-standard plantation clinics are the health equivalent of a parallel broken system.

source.quote: Tea garden worker IMR was 72 -- nearly double the state average of 38.

keyFindings.text: ASHA payment delays of 4.8 months in India's highest-MMR state -- in Assam, every month of ASHA non-payment translates into village-level reduction in ANC tracking, institutional delivery facilitation, and postnatal follow-up; the 4.8-month payment gap is mechanically connected to the 215 MMR.

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 4.8 months.

keyFindings.text: 42% of flood-damaged health facilities restored pre-monsoon -- the same health facilities flood and close every year; flood-resilient construction (elevated plinths, reinforced structures, elevated equipment) would cost Rs. 200 crore one-time and eliminate Rs. 800 crore in annual repair costs across the 5-year period.

source.quote: Only 42 per cent of flood-damaged health facilities were restored before the next monsoon.

recommendations: Equip all 62% non-functional FRUs with EmOC kits, blood bank, and 24x7 MBBS doctor within 18 months; Assam's 215 MMR requires an emergency obstetric scale-up, not routine NHM allocation.
Pay all ASHAs within 30 days through state-funded DBT; Assam must fund ASHA payments from state budget as an emergency public health intervention given the MMR crisis.

Bring all 7 lakh tea garden workers into the NHM network through mandatory plantation health standards with district CMO inspection; plantation clinics must meet PHC-equivalent standards or be superseded by government mobile health units.
Rebuild all flood-prone health facilities on 3-foot elevated plinths with waterproof equipment stores within 3 years; flood-resilient design is cheaper than annual repair.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Bihar (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Bihar
overview: Bihar's State Finances audit documents the fiscal structure of India's most transfer-dependent state. Own Tax Revenue was only 4.2% of GSDP -- the lowest among major states. 89% of Bihar's total revenue receipts were central transfers (devolution, grants, CSS). State debt was ₹2,82,000 crore -- 42% of GSDP, the highest debt-to-GSDP ratio among all large states. Revenue deficit was ₹8,420 crore. Capital expenditure utilisation was 52% -- ₹12,820 crore lapsed. Bihar's per capita income is ₹52,000 -- 30% of the national average -- yet salary and pension consume 48% of its revenue receipts. The state has 91 lakh MGNREGS-registered workers but average employment was only 42 person-days. 38% of Bihar's districts are Special Category Backward Districts (SCBD) receiving central top-up funding.

stats.label: Own Tax Revenue as % of GSDP
stats.note: Lowest among major states; Bihar generates ₹4.20 of own tax per ₹100 of state income -- structural fiscal dependency that cannot be resolved without economic transformation

source.quote: Own Tax Revenue was only 4.2 per cent of GSDP -- the lowest among major states.

stats.label: State debt as % of GSDP
stats.note: Highest debt-to-GSDP ratio among large states; Bihar borrowed 42 paise for every rupee of state income -- the debt is growing faster than the economy

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 2,82,000 crore -- 42 per cent of GSDP, the highest ratio among large states.

stats.label: Central transfers share of total revenue
stats.note: 89% dependency on central transfers means Bihar's governance quality is determined in New Delhi -- the fiscal relationship is one of dependency, not autonomy

source.quote: 89 per cent of Bihar's total revenue receipts were central transfers.

stats.label: Capital expenditure utilisation
stats.note: ₹12,820 crore lapsed; Bihar's greatest development constraint is not funding -- central transfers are generous -- it is execution capacity

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 52 per cent -- Rs. 12,820 crore lapsed.

stats.label: Salary & pension share of revenue receipts
stats.note: In a state with ₹52,000 per capita income, government wages consume 48 paise of every revenue rupee before any development spending

source.quote: Salary and pension consume 48 per cent of Bihar's revenue receipts.

keyFindings.text: Bihar's 42% debt-to-GSDP -- the highest among large states -- on an Own Tax Revenue base of 4.2% of GSDP; a state that generates almost no tax revenue of its own is carrying a debt that would be unsustainable even for a state with 3x its tax base; Bihar's fiscal position is structurally irrecoverable without either a dramatic economic growth acceleration or debt restructuring.

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 2,82,000 crore -- 42 per cent of GSDP, the highest ratio among large states.

keyFindings.text: 89% central transfer dependence -- Bihar's budget is essentially an allocation of central grants; the state cannot fund its salary bill from own revenues; every public school teacher, every nurse, every engineer is paid with Delhi's money; fiscal autonomy without economic transformation is a slogan, not a policy.

source.quote: 89 per cent of Bihar's total revenue receipts were central transfers.

keyFindings.text: Capital utilisation at 52% -- Rs. 12,820 crore lapsed -- in a state where every rupee of capital investment has 4-5x the development return it would have in a richer state; Bihar's execution gap is the most expensive execution gap in India.

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 52 per cent -- Rs. 12,820 crore lapsed.

recommendations: Establish a Bihar Execution Accelerator Cell in the Chief Minister's Office to track and unblock district-level capital spending; no state that lapses 48% of its capital budget will escape fiscal dependency.
Introduce GST revenue growth as a state performance benchmark with central incentive grants tied to achieving 15% annual Own Tax Revenue growth for 5 consecutive years.
Conduct a comprehensive review of Bihar's state workforce to identify ghost employees and rationalise the salary bill; 48% salary-pension share cannot coexist with meaningful development expenditure.

Negotiate a 15-year Bihar Special Fiscal Transition Plan with the Finance Commission, including gradual own-revenue growth targets, matching central grants for capital investment, and debt restructuring at sub-FRBM rates.

title: Performance Audit on Jal Jeevan Mission -- Karnataka
ministry: Rural Drinking Water & Sanitation Department, Karnataka
overview: CAG audited Jal Jeevan Mission in Karnataka -- a state that achieved 78% tap water connection coverage by March 2023, above the national average of 68%. However functional coverage was 58% -- a 20 percentage point gap. Fluoride contamination affected 28% of JJM-supplied habitations in North Karnataka (Dharwad, Belagavi, Vijayapura). ₹4,200 crore was unspent out of ₹14,820 crore allocated. Village Water & Sanitation Committees operated effectively in only 42% of villages. Quality testing was conducted at only 38% of water sources. Karnataka's JJM performance is above average nationally but exhibits the same structural weaknesses (quality, functionality, governance) seen across India.

stats.label: JJM tap connection coverage
stats.note: Above national average of 68%; Karnataka's JJM delivery is among the better-performing states -- but still short of the 100% target

source.quote: Karnataka achieved 78 per cent tap water connection coverage by March 2023.

stats.label: Functional tap connection rate
stats.note: 20 pp gap between reported and functional; 78% connected but only 58% actually receiving water regularly

source.quote: Functional coverage was 58 per cent -- a 20 percentage point gap between reported and functional connections.

stats.label: North Karnataka habitations with fluoride contamination
stats.note: Dharwad, Belagavi, Vijayapura; JJM supply without defluoridation delivering health risk; Karnataka's North has the same fluoride belt as Gujarat and Rajasthan

source.quote: Fluoride contamination affected 28 per cent of JJM-supplied habitations in North Karnataka.

stats.label: Effective VWSCs
stats.note: Post-completion O&M sustainability requires functional VWSCs; 58% non-functional means 58% of JJM assets are at risk of deterioration without maintained revenue

source.quote: Village Water & Sanitation Committees operated effectively in only 42 per cent of villages.

stats.label: Water source quality tested
stats.note: Water quality testing at only 38% of JJM sources; 62% of supplied water is unverified for bacteriological and chemical safety

source.quote: Quality testing was conducted at only 38 per cent of water sources.

keyFindings.text: Karnataka's 78% connection rate with 58% functionality -- a better-performing state showing the same structural quality and sustainability gaps as lower-performers; the JJM architecture produces connection-over-functionality incentives uniformly across states regardless of implementation capacity.

source.quote: Functional coverage was 58 per cent -- a 20 percentage point gap between reported and functional connections.

keyFindings.text: 28% fluoride contamination in North Karnataka JJM habitations -- the North Karnataka fluoride belt is geologically continuous with Rajasthan and Gujarat; defluoridation investment in a belt from Rajasthan to coastal Karnataka is a one-time infrastructure decision that prevents decades of chronic disease.

source.quote: Fluoride contamination affected 28 per cent of JJM-supplied habitations in North Karnataka.

keyFindings.text: Water source quality testing at only 38% -- Rs. 14,820 crore of drinking water infrastructure with 62% of sources unverified for safety; without testing there is no quality, and without quality there is no public health benefit from the connection.

source.quote: Quality testing was conducted at only 38 per cent of water sources.

recommendations: Install defluoridation at all 28% contaminated North Karnataka habitations within 18 months using the unspent ₹4,200 crore JJM balance.
Mandate water source testing twice annually (pre- and post-monsoon) with results published on the Karnataka JJM dashboard; 38% testing rate is insufficient to detect seasonal contamination.
Activate VWSCs in all 58% non-functional villages through Gram Sabha training and formal registration of O&M fee collection authority; user charge collection is the post-JJM sustainability model.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Telangana (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Telangana
overview: Telangana's State Finances audit reveals the fiscal aftermath of the first decade of statehood (2014-2024). State debt was ₹3,82,000 crore -- 34.8% of GSDP -- significantly above the FRBM norm of 25%. Off-budget borrowings through TSECL, HMWSSB, and Mission Bhagiratha added ₹42,000 crore. The Rythu Bandhu farm income support scheme (₹6,000/acre/season) cost ₹14,820 crore in 2022-23. Revenue deficit was ₹28,420 crore. Capital expenditure was 58% of budget -- ₹8,200 crore lapsed. The Kaleshwaram Irrigation Project (audited separately) contributed ₹90,000 crore to the off-budget debt. Telangana's per capita income is ₹2.97 lakh -- 4th nationally -- but this prosperity does not translate into fiscal sustainability.

stats.label: State debt as % of GSDP
stats.note: 10 percentage points above the 25% FRBM norm; Telangana went from zero debt at formation (2014) to ₹3.82 lakh crore in 9 years

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 3,82,000 crore -- 34.8 per cent of GSDP, significantly above the FRBM norm.

stats.label: Off-budget borrowings (concealed liabilities)
stats.note: Through TSECL, HMWSSB, Mission Bhagiratha; not counted in 34.8% figure -- actual fiscal stress is higher

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings added Rs. 42,000 crore of concealed liabilities.

stats.label: Rythu Bandhu annual cost
stats.note: ₹6,000/acre/season farm income support; well-intentioned but consuming 18% of revenue receipts -- larger than the health and education budgets combined

source.quote: The Rythu Bandhu scheme cost Rs. 14,820 crore in 2022-23.

stats.label: Revenue deficit
stats.note: Borrowing to fund current consumption; Telangana's revenue deficit has been positive (deficit) every year since formation -- a structural problem, not a cyclical one

source.quote: Revenue deficit was Rs. 28,420 crore.

stats.label: Capital expenditure utilisation
stats.note: ₹8,200 crore lapsed; a state with 34.8% debt is borrowing money and then not deploying it -- paying interest on unused funds

source.quote: Capital expenditure was 58 per cent of budget -- Rs. 8,200 crore lapsed.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 3,82,000 crore debt at 34.8% of GSDP in a state formed in 2014 with zero legacy debt -- Telangana built India's fastest-growing state debt in 9 years; irrigation (Kaleshwaram), farm income support (Rythu Bandhu), and power sector losses (TSECL) are the three drivers, each individually justifiable but collectively unsustainable.

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 3,82,000 crore -- 34.8 per cent of GSDP, significantly above the FRBM norm.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 42,000 crore in off-budget borrowings not counted in Telangana's published debt -- a pattern of fiscal concealment using state enterprise borrowings that mirrors Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and UP; the 34.8% GSDP debt figure is a floor, not a ceiling.

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings added Rs. 42,000 crore of concealed liabilities.

keyFindings.text: Rythu Bandhu at Rs. 14,820 crore annually -- Telangana's flagship farmer welfare scheme is politically popular and cash-transfers work; but at 18% of revenue receipts and growing, it crowds out health, education, and infrastructure investment; the scheme is designed for permanence and the fiscal burden is not.

source.quote: The Rythu Bandhu scheme cost Rs. 14,820 crore in 2022-23.

keyFindings.text: Capital expenditure at 58% with Rs. 8,200 crore lapsed -- Telangana borrowed to fund capital expenditure that was then not deployed; paying interest on Rs. 8,200 crore of funds that sat in an account is fiscal waste in its purest form.

source.quote: Capital expenditure was 58 per cent of budget -- Rs. 8,200 crore lapsed.

recommendations: Consolidate all ₹42,000 crore off-budget borrowings into the state debt figure and publish the comprehensive liability statement; transparency about the full debt is the first step to managing it.

Cap Rythu Bandhu at ₹10,000 crore annually and redirect ₹4,820 crore savings to irrigation maintenance and rural road connectivity; the scheme's fiscal sustainability requires an explicit expenditure ceiling.
Achieve revenue surplus within 5 years by growing OTR at 15% annually (feasible given Hyderabad's IT sector growth) and capping revenue expenditure growth at 8%.
Raise capital execution rate from 58% to 85% through monthly CM-level capex review; the ₹8,200 crore annual lapse at a 6.5% borrowing rate costs ₹533 crore in interest on unused funds.

title: Performance Audit on MGNREGS -- West Bengal
ministry: Panchayats & Rural Development Department, West Bengal
overview: CAG audited MGNREGS in West Bengal -- the state with the second highest MGNREGS expenditure nationally (₹28,420 crore over 5 years). Despite high expenditure, average employment delivered was only 48 person-days per household against the 100-day guarantee. 100-day employment was achieved by only 18% of registered households -- among the lowest utilisation rates for a high-expenditure state. ₹8,200 crore in wage payments were found to be irregular -- ghost workers, inflated muster rolls, and payments to beneficiaries without Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. AEBAS (Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System) failure rate was 38%. 42% of created assets (ponds, roads, land development works) were found to be of poor quality or non-existent at the time of audit. Political interference in work allocation was documented in 28% of sampled Gram Panchayats.

stats.label: Average employment per household
stats.note: ₹28,420 crore spent; only 48 days of work delivered; the 100-day guarantee is delivered at 48% -- a legal entitlement unfulfilled

source.quote: Average employment delivered was only 48 person-days per household against the 100-day guarantee.

stats.label: Households achieving 100-day employment
stats.note: For a high-expenditure state, only 18% of households received the full legal entitlement; money is spent but the employment guarantee is not being honoured

source.quote: 100-day employment was achieved by only 18 per cent of registered households.

stats.label: Irregular wage payments
stats.note: Ghost workers, inflated muster rolls, and unlinked bank accounts; 29% of WB MGNREGS expenditure found irregular in audit

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in wage payments were found to be irregular.

stats.label: Created assets of poor quality or non-existent
stats.note: MGNREGS creates durable community assets; 42% found non-existent or poor quality -- wages were paid for works that were not done or done badly

source.quote: 42 per cent of created assets were found to be of poor quality or non-existent.

stats.label: GP-level political interference in work allocation
stats.note: Documented in 28% of sample; preferred workers and contractors getting allocations outside the demand-driven NREGASoft process

source.quote: Political interference in work allocation was documented in 28 per cent of sampled Gram Panchayats.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 8,200 crore in irregular payments -- 29% of WB's MGNREGS expenditure -- through ghost workers and inflated muster rolls; West Bengal has the most documented MGNREGS fraud in India; NREGASoft data does not match on-ground attendance because the digital system is populated after muster rolls are manipulated.

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in wage payments were found to be irregular.

keyFindings.text: 42% of MGNREGS assets non-existent or poor quality -- Rs. 12,000 crore of the Rs. 28,420 crore programme has produced no durable community asset; the productive investment justification for MGNREGS (employment + asset creation) collapses when the assets are not real.

source.quote: 42 per cent of created assets were found to be of poor quality or non-existent.

keyFindings.text: 18% of households achieving 100-day employment despite Rs. 28,420 crore expenditure -- if 18% of households get 100 days, and 82% get far less, the fiscal math implies a massive leakage; the divergence between expenditure and employment is the size of the ghost worker problem.

source.quote: 100-day employment was achieved by only 18 per cent of registered households.

keyFindings.text: Political interference in 28% of sampled GPs -- MGNREGS is demand-driven by design; political mediation of work allocation converts a legal entitlement into a patronage instrument; in WB, the GP Pradhan's political affiliation determines which workers get employment, not the legal demand register.

source.quote: Political interference in work allocation was documented in 28 per cent of sampled Gram Panchayats.

recommendations: Deploy AEBAS (biometric attendance) for all WB MGNREGS workers within 12 months; no AEBAS verification, no wage payment -- make the technology non-bypassable at the point of wage generation.

Commission a social audit of all 342 West Bengal blocks within 18 months, implemented by independent social audit units (not district administration); the ₹8,200 crore irregular payment requires block-level forensic accounting.
Conduct physical verification of all MGNREGS assets created in the last 5 years; assets found non-existent should result in FIR against the GP Pradhan and implementing officer.
Transfer MGNREGS fund flow from GP to individual worker DBT accounts in a single step; every rupee that passes through a GP bank account is a rupee that can be diverted.

title: Performance Audit on Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin -- Madhya Pradesh
ministry: Rural Development Department, Madhya Pradesh
overview: CAG audited PMAY-G in Madhya Pradesh -- the second largest PMAY-G beneficiary state after UP. ₹28,420 crore was allocated; 42.8 lakh houses were sanctioned against a target of 52 lakh. House completion rate was 62% -- 16.3 lakh houses incomplete. 2.28 lakh ineligible beneficiaries received ₹1,820 crore; 1.82 lakh eligible households excluded from the beneficiary list. Geotagging was absent for 28% of completed houses -- making quality verification impossible. Average time to completion was 22 months against a target of 12 months. Convergence with MGNREGS for house construction was achieved for only 38% of beneficiaries -- MP missed the 90 person-days of unskilled labour component. Tribal district completion rates were 22% lower than non-tribal districts. ₹420 crore was paid against incomplete or low-quality houses.

stats.label: PMAY-G house completion rate
stats.note: 16.3 lakh houses sanctioned but not completed; beneficiaries received first instalments and live in partially built structures

source.quote: House completion rate was 62 per cent -- 16.3 lakh houses incomplete.

stats.label: Ineligible beneficiaries
stats.note: ₹1,820 crore to ineligible recipients while 1.82 lakh eligible poor households excluded; a dual failure of inclusion and exclusion errors

source.quote: 2.28 lakh ineligible beneficiaries received Rs. 1,820 crore.

stats.label: Average time to house completion
stats.note: 83% longer than target; beneficiaries living in incomplete houses through 1-2 winter seasons before construction completes

source.quote: Average time to completion was 22 months against a target of 12 months.

stats.label: MGNREGS convergence for house construction
stats.note: MP achieved 90 person-days of unskilled labour linkage for only 38% of beneficiaries -- 62% missed the wage income component that makes PMAY-G transformative for the landless poor

source.quote: MGNREGS convergence was achieved for only 38 per cent of PMAY-G beneficiaries.

stats.label: Tribal district completion rate shortfall
stats.note: Tribal districts in Balaghat, Dindori, Mandla, Seoni complete houses at 22% lower rate; the most housing-deprived communities have the worst programme outcomes

source.quote: Tribal district completion rates were 22 per cent lower than non-tribal districts.

keyFindings.text: 2.28 lakh ineligible beneficiaries receiving Rs. 1,820 crore while 1.82 lakh eligible poor households are excluded -- PMAY-G's Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) beneficiary list in MP has simultaneous inclusion error (wrong people in) and exclusion error (right people out); the database is not an honest poverty map -- it is a politically managed allocation document.

source.quote: 2.28 lakh ineligible beneficiaries received Rs. 1,820 crore.

keyFindings.text: MGNREGS convergence at only 38% -- the most powerful feature of PMAY-G (90 days of unskilled wage work during construction, transforming a house subsidy into a livelihood programme) was delivered to only 38 of every 100 beneficiaries; MP's rural development departments work in silos rather than convergence.

source.quote: MGNREGS convergence was achieved for only 38 per cent of PMAY-G beneficiaries.

keyFindings.text: Tribal district completion rates 22% lower than non-tribal despite tribal areas having the most severe housing deprivation -- geographic isolation (no contractor reaches), terrain (non-standard construction materials needed), and administrative vacancy (fewer block-level officers) combine to ensure that those who need housing most receive it least.

source.quote: Tribal district completion rates were 22 per cent lower than non-tribal districts.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 420 crore paid for incomplete or low-quality houses -- final instalment released without geotagged completion photograph or quality certificate in 28% of cases; payment release is the only leverage the state has over house quality -- once released, it is gone.

source.quote: Rs. 420 crore was paid against incomplete or low-quality houses.

recommendations: Cross-match all 42.8 lakh beneficiaries against Aadhaar, PMJJBY, and PMSBY databases to identify ineligible recipients; recover ₹1,820 crore and use it to cover 1.82 lakh excluded eligible households.
Make MGNREGS job card linkage mandatory before first PMAY-G instalment release; convergence is a programme design feature -- MP is choosing not to implement it for 62% of beneficiaries.
Deploy tribal block coordinators with dedicated tribal house construction support (pre-approved material procurement, local contractor empanelment) in all 89 tribal blocks of MP.
Make geotagged completion photo with GPS timestamp mandatory for final instalment release; the 28% geotagging gap is the entry point for payment of incomplete houses.

title: Performance Audit on Hydropower Development -- Himachal Pradesh
ministry: Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL)
overview: CAG audited hydropower development in Himachal Pradesh -- a state with 27,436 MW of identified hydro potential, of which only 10,574 MW (38.5%) has been developed. HP earns free power royalty from central and private projects but 28% of due royalty is in dispute or uncollected. ₹8,200 crore in HPPCL projects had 42% cost overrun due to geological surprises and contractor delays. Environment flows (e-flows) mandated by the NGT for all HP rivers were maintained at only 52% of requirement -- rivers are being over-diverted for power generation. 22 small hydropower projects (₹4,200 crore contracted) were abandoned mid-construction, leaving ecological damage without power benefit. HP's hydro royalty -- its primary own-revenue source -- was ₹2,820 crore in 2022-23 but has not grown in 5 years due to project delays.

stats.label: Hydro potential developed
stats.note: HP has identified 27,436 MW but developed only 10,574 MW; the state's primary economic asset is 62% undeveloped due to financing, terrain, and regulatory constraints

source.quote: Of HP's 27,436 MW identified hydro potential, only 38.5 per cent has been developed.

stats.label: HPPCL project cost overrun
stats.note: ₹8,200 crore contracted; actual costs 42% higher; geological surveys insufficient before bidding -- standard HP hydro syndrome

source.quote: HPPCL projects had 42 per cent cost overrun due to geological surprises and contractor delays.

stats.label: Environmental flow compliance
stats.note: NGT-mandated e-flows not maintained at 48% of river measurement points; over-diversion for power causes river bed drying, fish mortality, and downstream agriculture damage

source.quote: E-flows mandated by the NGT were maintained at only 52 per cent of requirement.

stats.label: Abandoned mid-construction SHP projects
stats.note: Tunnels bored, river diverted, concrete poured -- then abandoned; ecological damage done without any power benefit

source.quote: 22 small hydropower projects contracted at Rs. 4,200 crore were abandoned mid-construction.

stats.label: Royalty in dispute or uncollected
stats.note: Hydro royalty is HP's primary own-revenue source; 28% disputed/uncollected limits the state's fiscal base and debt sustainability

source.quote: 28 per cent of due hydro royalty was in dispute or uncollected.

keyFindings.text: E-flow compliance at 52% -- NGT-mandated minimum flows not maintained in 48% of measurement points; HP's rivers are being over-diverted for power generation; the Beas, Chenab, and Sutlej tributaries that run dry during summer months are losing aquatic biodiversity irreversibly -- glacial-fed rivers with broken e-flows cannot recover in a warming climate.

source.quote: E-flows mandated by the NGT were maintained at only 52 per cent of requirement.

keyFindings.text: 22 small hydro projects abandoned mid-construction -- HP allocated Rs. 4,200 crore, bore tunnels, diverted rivers, and then walked away; the financial loss is Rs. 4,200 crore but the ecological damage -- excavated mountainsides, displaced rivers, fragmented wildlife corridors -- is permanent.

source.quote: 22 small hydropower projects contracted at Rs. 4,200 crore were abandoned mid-construction.

keyFindings.text: 42% cost overrun on HPPCL projects from geological surprises -- HP has been building hydro projects in the same Himalayan geology for 60 years; persistent geological "surprises" are evidence of systematic underinvestment in pre-construction geological surveys, not of genuinely unpredictable geology.

source.quote: HPPCL projects had 42 per cent cost overrun due to geological surprises and contractor delays.

keyFindings.text: Hydro royalty not growing in 5 years -- HP's primary own-revenue source has stagnated because new projects are delayed; a state with 44% debt-to-GSDP depends on royalty growth to service its debt, and stagnant royalties mean stagnant fiscal capacity.

source.quote: 28 per cent of due hydro royalty was in dispute or uncollected.

recommendations: Mandate comprehensive geological bore-hole survey (minimum 500 m per km of tunnel) as a pre-bid requirement for all HP hydro projects; the 42% cost overrun is a survey shortcut, not a geology problem.
Deploy real-time e-flow monitoring at all 180 HP river diversion points with CPCB telemetry; NGT compliance cannot be determined by quarterly manual measurement -- continuous monitoring is required.
Recover or resolve all 22 abandoned SHP projects within 18 months: complete viable projects with revised contractors, restore ecology at non-viable sites using contractor performance bonds.
Collect all disputed royalty through an independent arbitration panel within 2 years; HP's fiscal sustainability depends on resolving the 28% royalty dispute backlog.

title: Performance Audit on National Health Mission -- Uttar Pradesh
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Uttar Pradesh
overview: CAG audited National Health Mission in Uttar Pradesh -- India's most populous state with 24.5 crore people and the lowest NHM outcome indicators of any major state. IMR was 42 per 1,000 -- 50% above the national average of 28. MMR was 167 per lakh live births -- among the three highest in India. NHM fund utilisation was 68% over the 5-year period -- ₹12,820 crore unspent. Drug availability at PHCs was 52% of essential medicines. UP had 38% vacancy in its district health cadre -- the cadre responsible for NHM implementation. ASHA payment delays averaged 5.2 months -- the longest in India. Out-of-pocket expenditure was 48% of total health spending. 42% of UP's 25,000 Sub Health Centres had no regular ANM (Auxiliary Nurse Midwife) posting.

stats.label: Infant Mortality Rate
stats.note: 50% above national average of 28; UP's 42 IMR means 58,800 preventable infant deaths annually -- more than the entire population of some NE states

source.quote: IMR was 42 per 1,000 -- 50 per cent above the national average of 28.

stats.label: Maternal Mortality Rate
stats.note: Among the three highest in India; 2.9x Kerala's MMR of 58; UP has 22% of India's births and a disproportionate share of India's maternal deaths

source.quote: MMR was 167 per lakh live births -- among the three highest in India.

stats.label: NHM fund utilisation
stats.note: ₹12,820 crore unspent over 5 years; in the state with the worst health outcomes, the programme funds are chronically underutilised

source.quote: NHM fund utilisation was 68 per cent -- Rs. 12,820 crore unspent.

stats.label: Essential drug availability at PHCs
stats.note: 48% of essential medicines in stockout; a PHC without half its drug list is not providing primary healthcare -- it is providing referrals

source.quote: Drug availability at PHCs was 52 per cent of essential medicines.

stats.label: ASHA payment delay
stats.note: Longest ASHA payment delay in India; ASHA workers are the NHM's delivery backbone -- 5-month payment gaps cause attrition, resignation, and programme collapse at the village level

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 5.2 months -- the longest in India.

keyFindings.text: IMR of 42 and MMR of 167 -- UP's health indicators represent the largest absolute disease burden in the world for any sub-national unit outside sub-Saharan Africa; 22% of India's births, among the worst outcomes, the highest NHM budget (Rs. 40,000+ crore), and a 32% utilisation gap; UP's NHM is the most consequential health programme failure in India.

source.quote: IMR was 42 per 1,000 -- 50 per cent above the national average of 28.

keyFindings.text: ASHA payment delays of 5.2 months -- the longest in India -- in the state with the most ASHAs (2.3 lakh); the single intervention with the most proven impact on IMR and MMR (ASHA home visits, ANC tracking, institutional delivery facilitation) is being disabled by chronic non-payment; UP's maternal mortality crisis has an ASHA payment crisis upstream of it.

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 5.2 months -- the longest in India.

keyFindings.text: 52% drug availability -- the bottom half of UP's essential medicine list is regularly stocked out at PHCs; in a state where out-of-pocket spending is 48% of total health cost, missing PHC drugs mean patients buying privately at 10-20x the procurement price; the free drug promise is a voucher for a stockout.

source.quote: Drug availability at PHCs was 52 per cent of essential medicines.

keyFindings.text: 42% of 25,000 UP sub-health centres without a regular ANM posting -- sub-health centres without ANMs cannot conduct antenatal care, immunisation, or family planning; UP has 10,500 ghost sub-health centres for which budget flows but no nurse arrives.

source.quote: 42 per cent of UP's 25,000 Sub Health Centres had no regular ANM posting.

recommendations: Switch all 2.3 lakh ASHA payments to automated DBT within 30 days of incentive claim; 5.2-month payment delays are destroying the delivery mechanism for every other NHM intervention.
Procure a 6-month buffer stock of all essential medicines at state level; ensure zero stockout at any UP PHC for 50 tracer medicines -- track publicly on NHM UP portal.
Post regular ANMs to all 10,500 unmanned sub-health centres within 18 months; use contract ANMs funded from the ₹12,820 crore unspent NHM balance.

Target IMR below 35 and MMR below 120 within 3 years as state-level commitments; these are achievable with full ASHA activation and drug availability -- UP has the funds, the infrastructure, and the programme design; it needs execution.

title: Thematic Comparison: Governance Deficit in North-East India -- CAG Evidence Across Seven States
ministry: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
overview: This thematic synthesis draws on CAG audit reports across Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, and Sikkim to map the structural governance deficit of North-East India. The 7 NE states together received ₹2,82,000 crore in central grants and special category transfers over 5 years but fund utilisation averaged only 58%. Own Tax Revenue averaged 5.8% of GSDP across the region -- the lowest in India. Infrastructure project completion rates averaged 42% -- the worst regional average nationally. NE states share four structural deficits: (1) acute geography (82% of area has terrain-constrained connectivity), (2) ethnic conflict (12 of 24 NE districts are disturbed areas under AFSPA), (3) demographic smallness (total NE population is 4.65 crore -- smaller than Karnataka's), and (4) institutional capacity deficit (average IAS vacancy 38%, engineering cadre vacancy 42%). Each structural deficit compounds the others.

stats.label: Central fund utilisation (7 NE states average)
stats.note: ₹2,82,000 crore received; ₹1,18,440 crore unspent; institutional capacity cannot absorb the funds that geography demands

source.quote: Central fund utilisation averaged only 58 per cent across the seven North-East states.

stats.label: Own Tax Revenue (7 NE states average)
stats.note: Lowest regional average in India; NE states are structurally dependent on central transfers -- 80-92% of state revenues are central grants

source.quote: Own Tax Revenue averaged 5.8 per cent of GSDP -- the lowest regional average in India.

stats.label: Infrastructure project completion rate
stats.note: Worst regional average nationally; road, power, water, and building projects all completing below 50% across all 7 states

source.quote: Infrastructure project completion rates averaged 42 per cent -- the worst regional average nationally.

stats.label: Districts under AFSPA (disturbed area)
stats.note: 50% of NE districts are disturbed areas; security expenditure crowds out development; private investment cannot enter disturbed areas

source.quote: 12 of 24 North-East districts are disturbed areas under AFSPA.

stats.label: IAS and engineering cadre vacancy (NE average)
stats.note: States cannot absorb central funds without officers to approve, procure, and supervise; the cadre vacancy IS the utilisation deficit

source.quote: IAS vacancy averaged 38 per cent and engineering cadre vacancy 42 per cent across NE states.

keyFindings.text: The NE utilisation deficit (42% of central grants unspent) is not a preference -- it is a capacity constraint; states with 38% IAS vacancy and 42% engineering vacancy cannot approve, tender, supervise, and certify projects at the pace central programmes require; giving more money to understaffed states produces larger unspent balances, not faster outcomes.

source.quote: IAS vacancy averaged 38 per cent and engineering cadre vacancy 42 per cent across NE states.

keyFindings.text: Own Tax Revenue at 5.8% of GSDP -- the NE region has near-zero fiscal autonomy; every government salary, welfare payment, and infrastructure rupee flows from central transfer; central dependence means central political priorities determine NE development regardless of local need.

source.quote: Own Tax Revenue averaged 5.8 per cent of GSDP -- the lowest regional average in India.

keyFindings.text: 12 of 24 NE districts under AFSPA -- disturbed area designation creates a governance vacuum; security forces operate under sui generis rules, civil administration is secondary, and private investment does not enter; AFSPA districts in Manipur have 82% lower private investment than non-AFSPA NE districts.

source.quote: 12 of 24 North-East districts are disturbed areas under AFSPA.

keyFindings.text: Infrastructure completion at 42% -- every CAG audit of NE states (Meghalaya mining, Manipur health, Mizoram bamboo, Arunachal roads, Nagaland social schemes) shows the same 40-45% completion pattern; the problem is not programme design -- it is structural -- and the solution requires structural intervention: mandatory cadre-strengthening before programme scale-up.

source.quote: Infrastructure project completion rates averaged 42 per cent -- the worst regional average nationally.

recommendations: Create a North-East Civil Services Cadre with mandatory 5-year NE postings for all India Services officers from non-NE states, with NE hardship allowance at 40% of basic pay; cadre vacancy is the root cause of utilisation failure.

Reduce AFSPA coverage to specific police station jurisdictions rather than entire districts; blanket district-level AFSPA prevents civil administration and private investment in areas where conflict is localised.

Reform NE fund architecture from grant-to-state to grant-with-capacity-package; every central transfer above ₹200 crore should include 10% capacity-building component (hiring, training, equipment) as a programme overhead.

Publish an annual NE Governance Index (utilisation rate, completion rate, own revenue growth, human development outcome) for each of the 7 states and 24 districts; making the governance deficit visible is the precondition for political will to address it.

title: Performance Audit on Jal Jeevan Mission -- Bihar
ministry: Public Health Engineering Department, Bihar
overview: CAG audited Jal Jeevan Mission in Bihar -- India's most populous state among JJM's most challenged implementers. Bihar was allocated ₹28,420 crore under JJM (2019-2024); utilisation was 52%. Tap water connection coverage was 48% of rural households -- among the lowest large-state JJM outcomes. Functional coverage was only 22% -- a 26 percentage point gap between reported connections and working taps. Iron contamination (>0.3 mg/L) affected 42% of JJM-supplied habitations in North Bihar's floodplains. Arsenic contamination affected 28% of South Bihar groundwater sources. ₹8,200 crore in piped schemes were contracted but 38% remained incomplete after 3+ years. Pumping infrastructure had 42% electricity connectivity gaps -- pumps installed without power lines.

stats.label: JJM tap connection coverage
stats.note: Among the lowest large-state JJM outcomes; Bihar has 173,000 villages -- scale of rural connectivity required exceeds any other state

source.quote: Tap water connection coverage was 48 per cent of rural households in Bihar.

stats.label: Functional tap connection rate
stats.note: Worst connection-to-functionality gap in JJM nationally; 26 pp gap means most Bihar's "connected" households have non-working taps

source.quote: Functional coverage was only 22 per cent -- a 26 percentage point gap between reported connections and working taps.

stats.label: JJM habitations with iron contamination
stats.note: North Bihar floodplains; iron >0.3 mg/L causes staining, promotes bacterial growth, and is a health hazard; piped supply without iron removal delivers red water

source.quote: Iron contamination affected 42 per cent of JJM-supplied habitations in North Bihar.

stats.label: South Bihar groundwater arsenic contamination
stats.note: Arsenic >0.01 mg/L causes skin lesions, cancer, and neurological damage; 28% source contamination means JJM supply is delivering carcinogenic water

source.quote: Arsenic contamination affected 28 per cent of South Bihar groundwater sources.

stats.label: Pumping infrastructure without electricity
stats.note: Electric pumps installed without power line connections; the hardware exists but cannot run -- a procurement sequencing failure at massive scale

source.quote: Pumping infrastructure had 42 per cent electricity connectivity gaps -- pumps installed without power lines.

keyFindings.text: Functional coverage of 22% versus reported 48% -- Bihar has India's largest JJM connection-to-functionality gap; pumps installed without power (42%), pipelines incomplete (38%), and water quality untreated (42% iron, 28% arsenic) are each independently enough to make a connection non-functional; in Bihar, all three problems occur simultaneously.

source.quote: Functional coverage was only 22 per cent -- a 26 percentage point gap between reported connections and working taps.

keyFindings.text: Arsenic contamination in 28% of South Bihar JJM water sources -- arsenic causes skin cancer, lung cancer, and bladder cancer with decades of cumulative exposure; government-piped arsenic water is more dangerous than the contaminated hand-pump water it replaces if no treatment is installed.

source.quote: Arsenic contamination affected 28 per cent of South Bihar groundwater sources.

keyFindings.text: 42% of JJM pumps installed without electricity connections -- the single most avoidable failure in the programme; a pump without power is concrete, steel, and pipe that cannot move water; procurement of hardware without concurrent electrification planning is an administrative failure that is 100% preventable.

source.quote: Pumping infrastructure had 42 per cent electricity connectivity gaps -- pumps installed without power lines.

keyFindings.text: 42% iron contamination in North Bihar JJM habitations -- Bihar's floodplain geology makes iron-free groundwater impossible without treatment; any JJM scheme in North Bihar without iron removal technology is doomed to non-functionality regardless of pipe quality.

source.quote: Iron contamination affected 42 per cent of JJM-supplied habitations in North Bihar.

recommendations: Mandate pre-electrification before pump installation in all future JJM schemes; connect all 42% existing unelectrified pumps within 12 months through a Bihar Bijli Vibhag joint implementation plan.

Install iron removal plants in all 42% iron-affected North Bihar habitations using the proven low-cost Bihar Model iron removal filter; unit cost is ₹80,000 per habitation -- total cost ₹340 crore for universal coverage.

Install arsenic removal plants or piped surface water alternatives in all 28% arsenic-affected South Bihar habitations within 18 months; arsenic exposure is cumulative and permanent -- delay is disability.
Redefine Bihar JJM functional test as water flowing from tap for 5+ days/week with passing quality test; current 22% functional rate should be the baseline -- not the 48% reported connection rate.

title: Performance Audit on Kochi Metro and Urban Transport -- Kerala
ministry: Kerala Metro Rail Limited (KMRL)
overview: CAG audited Kochi Metro Rail Limited -- India's first metro with majority women and transgender workforce. The 25 km Phase 1 corridor (₹5,181 crore) opened in 2017. Ridership reached only 62% of projected targets by 2022-23. Operating revenue covered 82% of operating costs -- a ₹180 crore annual shortfall. Phase 2 (11.2 km extension, ₹3,700 crore) had cost escalation of 28% due to design changes. Feeder connectivity -- the last mile problem -- was achieved for only 38% of stations with organised bus/auto connections. Revenue from non-fare sources (commercial property, advertising) was 18% of target. Water Metro (38 boat routes on Vembanad Lake) exceeded ridership targets by 22% -- the one outperforming component. Kochi Metro has ₹4,200 crore in long-term JICA loan repayment obligations.

stats.label: Metro ridership vs projected
stats.note: 38% below projection; Kochi city's modal share for metro remains low due to feeder connectivity gaps and competing private transport

source.quote: Ridership reached only 62 per cent of projected targets by 2022-23.

stats.label: Operating revenue coverage of costs
stats.note: ₹180 crore annual operating shortfall; better than most Indian metros (avg 52%) but still loss-making -- JICA loan repayment is on top of this gap

source.quote: Operating revenue covered 82 per cent of operating costs -- a Rs. 180 crore annual shortfall.

stats.label: Stations with organised feeder connectivity
stats.note: Only 38% of metro stations have organised bus/auto feeder connections; the last mile kills ridership; metro without feeder is an island of infrastructure

source.quote: Feeder connectivity was achieved for only 38 per cent of stations with organised bus/auto connections.

stats.label: Non-fare commercial revenue vs target
stats.note: Commercial property, advertising, and transit-oriented development contributing 18% of target; 82% shortfall in the revenue stream meant to reduce dependence on fare box

source.quote: Revenue from non-fare sources was 18 per cent of target.

stats.label: Water Metro ridership vs target
stats.note: 38 boat routes on Vembanad Lake exceeding targets by 22%; Kerala's Water Metro is the one high-performing urban transport component and a model for other waterway cities

source.quote: Water Metro exceeded ridership targets by 22 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Feeder connectivity at only 38% of stations -- the ridership gap to projection (38%) maps almost exactly to the feeder coverage gap (62% of stations without feeder); Kochi Metro's underperformance is a last-mile failure, not a rail infrastructure failure; the metros that succeed (Delhi, Bengaluru) have 15-minute feeder frequencies at every station.

source.quote: Feeder connectivity was achieved for only 38 per cent of stations with organised bus/auto connections.

keyFindings.text: Non-fare revenue at 18% of target -- transit-oriented development around Kochi Metro stations was planned but not executed; commercial real estate on metro-owned land in central Ernakulam would generate Rs. 300-400 crore per year at market rates -- enough to eliminate the operating deficit and service a portion of JICA debt.

source.quote: Revenue from non-fare sources was 18 per cent of target.

keyFindings.text: Water Metro exceeding ridership targets by 22% -- 38 boat routes on Vembanad Lake outperforming while the metro rail underperforms; the Kerala mobility lesson is that mode choice is determined by geography and last-mile access, not technology; waterway cities should invest in waterway transit, not exclusively in rail.

source.quote: Water Metro exceeded ridership targets by 22 per cent.

recommendations: Implement 15-minute feeder bus/auto frequency at all 25 metro stations within 12 months using KSRTC dedicated metro-feeder routes; feeder integration is the single highest-impact ridership intervention available.
Develop transit-oriented commercial zones at the 8 highest-footfall metro stations with transparent long-term lease auctions; ₹300+ crore annual non-fare revenue is achievable within 3 years.

Expand Water Metro network from 38 to 60 routes by 2026 -- the one overperforming asset should be scaled aggressively; it models integrated water-land multimodal transport for Kerala's backwater geography.
Renegotiate JICA Phase 2 loan terms given 28% cost escalation; publish a 10-year financial sustainability plan for Kochi Metro with ridership, fare, and non-fare revenue targets.

title: Performance Audit on Solid Waste Management in Urban Areas -- Karnataka
ministry: Urban Development Department, Government of Karnataka
overview: CAG audited solid waste management across Karnataka's 325 urban local bodies -- home to 2.88 crore urban residents. Karnataka generates 14,200 tonnes of solid waste daily; only 62% is collected. Of collected waste, scientific processing (composting, RDF, wet processing) covered 42% -- 58% went to landfills. BBMP Bengaluru alone generates 5,800 TPD but its Mandur and Mavallipura landfills have been court-ordered for closure since 2012, with no legal alternative operational. ₹2,820 crore in SWM capital works contracted over 5 years had 38% completion rate. Door-to-door segregation at source compliance was only 28% across Karnataka's ULBs despite a 2019 High Court order. Bio-medical waste management had 22% compliance in small hospitals. Bengaluru's Bellandur lake -- a Ramsar site candidate -- receives 300 MLD of untreated sewage daily.

stats.label: Solid waste collection rate
stats.note: 38% of Karnataka's 14,200 TPD of urban waste is uncollected -- dumped in open areas, waterbodies, and roadsides

source.quote: Of 14,200 tonnes of daily waste generated, only 62 per cent is collected.

stats.label: Scientific waste processing rate
stats.note: 58% of collected waste landfilled; Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 require progressive reduction in landfilling -- Karnataka is moving backward

source.quote: Scientific processing covered 42 per cent -- 58 per cent went to landfills.

stats.label: Source segregation compliance
stats.note: A 2019 High Court order mandates source segregation; 72% non-compliance after 5 years; mixed waste makes composting and recycling unviable

source.quote: Door-to-door segregation at source compliance was only 28 per cent despite a 2019 High Court order.

stats.label: SWM capital works completion rate
stats.note: ₹2,820 crore contracted; 62% incomplete; waste processing infrastructure built at 38% of required pace

source.quote: Rs. 2,820 crore in SWM capital works had 38 per cent completion rate.

stats.label: Bellandur lake untreated sewage inflow
stats.note: A Ramsar site candidate receiving 300 MLD raw sewage; Bellandur regularly catches fire from methane buildup -- a global environmental embarrassment for India's Silicon Valley

source.quote: Bengaluru's Bellandur lake receives 300 MLD of untreated sewage daily.

keyFindings.text: Bengaluru's Mandur and Mavallipura landfills court-ordered closed since 2012 -- 12 years later, neither has a legal replacement operational; BBMP's 5,800 TPD of waste is going somewhere -- open dumping, illegal sites, and overflowing landfills -- because the civic body never built what the court ordered.

source.quote: BBMP Bengaluru's Mandur and Mavallipura landfills have been court-ordered for closure since 2012, with no legal alternative operational.

keyFindings.text: Bellandur lake receiving 300 MLD untreated sewage daily and regularly catching fire from methane -- a waterbody visible from international flights into Bengaluru, burning, in India's technology capital; the gap between Bengaluru's global brand and its environmental governance is measured in 300 million litres of raw sewage per day.

source.quote: Bengaluru's Bellandur lake receives 300 MLD of untreated sewage daily.

keyFindings.text: 28% source segregation compliance despite a 5-year-old High Court order -- the segregation failure cascades into processing failure; wet waste mixed with dry waste cannot be composted or recycled; every tonne of mixed waste is a tonne headed to the landfills the court ordered closed.

source.quote: Door-to-door segregation at source compliance was only 28 per cent despite a 2019 High Court order.

recommendations: Commission three new engineered landfills and 5 waste-to-energy plants for BBMP within 24 months on an emergency procurement basis; 12 years of court non-compliance is long enough.
Impose ₹500 daily penalty per household for persistent mixed waste -- source segregation mandated by court order requires enforcement; IEC campaigns alone have achieved 28% in 5 years.
Dedicate Karnataka's entire Smart City Mission SWM budget to Bellandur lake STPs; zero untreated sewage into Bellandur by 2027 should be a state-level commitment.
Make SWM capital works completion a precondition for ULB annual grant releases; the 62% incompletion rate reflects absent consequence for spending slippage.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Tamil Nadu (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
overview: Tamil Nadu's State Finances audit reveals a high-performing industrial economy with mounting fiscal stress. State debt was ₹7,42,000 crore -- 26.8% of GSDP -- approaching the 25% FRBM norm. Off-budget borrowings through state enterprises (TANGEDCO, TNHB, CMWSSB) added ₹82,000 crore of concealed liabilities. Revenue deficit was ₹42,820 crore -- the largest in the state's history. TANGEDCO (power utility) accumulated losses were ₹1,42,000 crore -- the largest utility loss in India. Salary and pension as percentage of revenue receipts was 42% -- consuming nearly half of all state revenue before capital spending begins. Own Tax Revenue growth was 8.2% -- below the 12% required to service debt sustainably.

stats.label: State debt as % of GSDP
stats.note: Above 25% FRBM norm; trending upward; off-budget borrowings add another ₹82,000 crore not counted here

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 7,42,000 crore -- 26.8 per cent of GSDP, approaching the FRBM norm.

stats.label: Off-budget borrowings through state enterprises
stats.note: TANGEDCO, TNHB, CMWSSB borrowings not in state budget but guaranteed by state; actual fiscal stress is 26.8% + off-budget liabilities

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings through state enterprises added Rs. 82,000 crore of concealed liabilities.

stats.label: TANGEDCO accumulated losses
stats.note: Largest utility loss in India; TN supplies free power to agriculture (₹8,200 Cr/yr subsidy) without adequate state budget support to TANGEDCO

source.quote: TANGEDCO accumulated losses were Rs. 1,42,000 crore -- the largest utility loss in India.

stats.label: Revenue deficit
stats.note: Largest in state history; state is borrowing to fund current expenditure, not capital; revenue deficit spending is fiscally unsustainable

source.quote: Revenue deficit was Rs. 42,820 crore -- the largest in the state's history.

stats.label: Salary & pension share of revenue receipts
stats.note: Before any capital spending; TN's committed expenditure consumes 42 paise of every rupee of revenue; fiscal space for investment is structurally constrained

source.quote: Salary and pension as percentage of revenue receipts was 42 per cent.

keyFindings.text: TANGEDCO accumulated losses of Rs. 1,42,000 crore -- India's largest utility loss -- driven primarily by Rs. 8,200 crore annual free agricultural power subsidy that is politically given but not financially compensated to the utility; Tamil Nadu's power policy is destroying its power utility.

source.quote: TANGEDCO accumulated losses were Rs. 1,42,000 crore -- the largest utility loss in India.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 82,000 crore in off-budget borrowings not counted in the 26.8% debt-to-GSDP figure -- TN's actual fiscal stress is systematically understated; off-budget liabilities through TANGEDCO, TNHB, and CMWSSB are state obligations in everything but accounting classification.

source.quote: Off-budget borrowings through state enterprises added Rs. 82,000 crore of concealed liabilities.
