keyFindings.text: Revenue deficit of Rs. 42,820 crore -- Tamil Nadu is borrowing to pay salaries and pensions, not to build roads and hospitals; when revenue deficit is the largest in state history, every rupee of infrastructure debt is competing with consumption debt for the same fiscal space.

source.quote: Revenue deficit was Rs. 42,820 crore -- the largest in the state's history.

keyFindings.text: 42% of revenue receipts consumed by salaries and pensions before any capital allocation -- TN's 11th Pay Commission implementation added Rs. 28,000 crore to the committed salary bill; the salary-pension commitment is growing faster than the tax base that funds it.

source.quote: Salary and pension as percentage of revenue receipts was 42 per cent.

recommendations: Transfer full agricultural power subsidy cost from TANGEDCO to state budget -- ₹8,200 crore annual subsidy must be a transparent fiscal line, not a hidden utility loss; TANGEDCO's ₹1.4 lakh crore loss is the cumulative cost of 20 years of off-budget agricultural subsidy.
Consolidate all ₹82,000 crore off-budget borrowings into the state debt figure for FRBM compliance; transparency about the full liability is the first step to managing it.
Achieve revenue surplus within 4 years by capping salary growth at 6% per annum and growing Own Tax Revenue at 14% per annum through property tax digitisation and GST compliance drives.
Implement UDAY-style TANGEDCO restructuring: state takes over 75% of TANGEDCO debt, TANGEDCO commits to AT&C losses below 15% and tariff rationalisation within 3 years.

title: Performance Audit on National Health Mission -- Andhra Pradesh
ministry: Health, Medical & Family Welfare Department, Andhra Pradesh
overview: CAG audited National Health Mission in Andhra Pradesh -- a state that reorganised its health system post-bifurcation from Telangana in 2014, rebuilding infrastructure from near zero. Despite ₹12,820 crore in NHM expenditure over 5 years and the flagship YSR Aarogyasri health insurance scheme (₹5 lakh cover), out-of-pocket expenditure remained 42% of total health spending. Drug availability at government hospitals was 68% -- 32% of essential medicines regularly stocked out. 22% of NHM sub-centres were single-nurse facilities with no doctor within 10 km. ASHA worker vacancy was 28%. AP's IMR was 28 per 1,000 -- close to national average -- but non-communicable disease burden (diabetes, hypertension) was rising at 18% annually with primary care absorption of only 38%.

stats.label: Out-of-pocket health expenditure
stats.note: Despite YSR Aarogyasri ₹5 lakh insurance; families still paying 42% of health costs out of pocket -- insurance covers hospitalisation not primary care

source.quote: Out-of-pocket expenditure remained 42 per cent of total health spending despite Aarogyasri.

stats.label: Essential drug availability at govt hospitals
stats.note: 32% of essential medicines in stockout; patients with Aarogyasri coverage cannot use insurance if medicines are unavailable at empanelled hospitals

source.quote: Drug availability at government hospitals was 68 per cent of essential medicines.

stats.label: NCD primary care absorption rate
stats.note: Diabetes and hypertension growing 18% per year; 62% of NCD cases reaching primary care are referred up or untreated -- the NCD tsunami will overwhelm tertiary hospitals

source.quote: Primary care absorption of NCD burden was only 38 per cent as NCDs rose 18 per cent annually.

stats.label: Sub-centres as single-nurse with no near doctor
stats.note: 22% of sub-centres are a nurse without physician backup within 10 km; for obstetric emergencies and NCD crises, this is a death zone

source.quote: 22 per cent of NHM sub-centres were single-nurse facilities with no doctor within 10 km.

stats.label: ASHA worker vacancy
stats.note: One in four ASHA positions unfilled; coverage gaps in Krishna, Guntur, and Vizianagaram districts most severe

source.quote: ASHA worker vacancy was 28 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Out-of-pocket health expenditure at 42% despite YSR Aarogyasri Rs. 5 lakh insurance -- the scheme covers hospitalisation but not primary care; 80% of health interactions are outpatient, and 100% of those are out-of-pocket; the flagship scheme protects against catastrophic hospitalisation but leaves routine care fully uninsured.

source.quote: Out-of-pocket expenditure remained 42 per cent of total health spending despite Aarogyasri.

keyFindings.text: NCD primary care absorption at 38% as diabetes and hypertension grow 18% annually -- AP's primary health system was designed for infectious disease and maternal health; it is structurally unprepared for a population that is ageing and urbanising rapidly; the NCD backpressure will reach AP's tertiary hospitals by 2028-30.

source.quote: Primary care absorption of NCD burden was only 38 per cent as NCDs rose 18 per cent annually.

keyFindings.text: 22% of AP sub-centres as single nurses with no doctor within 10 km -- for a pregnant woman in Alluri Sitharama Raju district going into complicated labour, a sub-centre nurse without physician backup is not a health facility; it is a delay before referral to a hospital that may be 2 hours away.

source.quote: 22 per cent of NHM sub-centres were single-nurse facilities with no doctor within 10 km.

recommendations: Extend YSR Aarogyasri to include outpatient NCD care with a defined benefit package (drugs, diagnostics, and consultation for diabetes and hypertension) funded through a ₹2,000/family/year premium top-up.
Increase drug availability to 95% through a state-owned emergency procurement buffer; use unspent NHM funds for a 6-month essential medicine stock.
Upgrade all 22% isolated sub-centres with telemedicine-connected doctor consultation and drug dispensing by 2026; no sub-centre should operate without physician access -- physical or virtual.
Deploy 28% ASHA vacancies within 12 months with priority in NCD-high districts; link ASHA incentive structure to NCD screening and follow-up outcomes.

title: Performance Audit on Jal Jeevan Mission -- Rajasthan
ministry: Public Health Engineering Department, Rajasthan
overview: CAG audited Jal Jeevan Mission in Rajasthan -- the most water-scarce large state in India, where 33 of 50 districts are designated dark zones for groundwater over-extraction. ₹22,420 crore was allocated under JJM; utilisation was 58%. Tap water connection coverage was 52% of rural households, but functional coverage (water actually delivered) was only 28% -- worse than the national JJM average. Fluoride contamination affected 38% of JJM-supplied villages. ₹4,200 crore in new piped infrastructure was built over aquifers that are already depleted -- water sources will fail within 5-8 years. Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) were non-functional in 62% of villages, breaking the community ownership model that JJM depends on.

stats.label: JJM fund utilisation
stats.note: ₹9,397 crore unspent in the most water-scarce large state; execution failure in the programme most critical to Rajasthan's water future

source.quote: JJM fund utilisation was 58 per cent in Rajasthan.

stats.label: Functional tap connection coverage
stats.note: Reported 52% coverage; only 28% functional; worst gap in India between reported and actual water access under JJM

source.quote: Functional coverage was only 28 per cent -- Rajasthan has the worst gap between reported and actual JJM coverage.

stats.label: JJM-supplied villages with fluoride contamination
stats.note: New piped supply connected to fluoride-contaminated groundwater; JJM is delivering a health risk alongside water access

source.quote: Fluoride contamination affected 38 per cent of JJM-supplied villages.

stats.label: Infrastructure over depleted aquifers
stats.note: Built without hydrogeological assessment; water sources expected to fail within 5-8 years -- stranded investment and future water insecurity

source.quote: Rs. 4,200 crore in new piped infrastructure was built over aquifers that are already depleted.

stats.label: Non-functional Village Water Committees
stats.note: VWSCs are JJM's community ownership mechanism; non-functional in 62% of Rajasthan villages -- the post-completion sustainability model has already collapsed

source.quote: Village Water & Sanitation Committees were non-functional in 62 per cent of villages.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 4,200 crore of JJM infrastructure built over already-depleted aquifers without hydrogeological assessment -- Rajasthan is building water pipes to sources that will fail within 5-8 years; infrastructure investment without source sustainability planning is money buried in a drying aquifer.

source.quote: Rs. 4,200 crore in new piped infrastructure was built over aquifers that are already depleted.

keyFindings.text: Functional coverage of 28% versus reported 52% -- Rajasthan's JJM coverage gap is the largest in India; connections reported as complete that deliver water intermittently or not at all; the measurement methodology that drives national JJM progress reports is unreliable.

source.quote: Functional coverage was only 28 per cent -- Rajasthan has the worst gap between reported and actual JJM coverage.

keyFindings.text: Fluoride contamination in 38% of JJM-supplied villages -- new government-built water infrastructure delivering fluoride-contaminated water; in a state where 12 lakh people already have fluorosis, JJM is expanding the disease burden rather than reducing it.

source.quote: Fluoride contamination affected 38 per cent of JJM-supplied villages.

keyFindings.text: Village Water Committees non-functional in 62% of villages -- JJM's sustainability model requires community-managed O&M post-completion; without functional VWSCs, piped infrastructure will deteriorate within 3 years of commissioning, repeating the handpump abandonment pattern of the 1990s.

source.quote: Village Water & Sanitation Committees were non-functional in 62 per cent of villages.

recommendations: Mandate hydrogeological assessment for all new JJM schemes before DPR approval; no scheme over depleted aquifers without alternative source development (rainwater harvesting, surface water linkage).
Redefine JJM functional connection as one delivering water 5 days per week minimum; measure and report functional rate, not connection rate -- ₹22,420 crore deserves honest outcome measurement.
Install defluoridation in all 38% of JJM villages with fluoride contamination within 18 months; use unspent JJM funds for treatment infrastructure.

Train and activate VWSCs in all 62% non-functional villages within 12 months; community management of O&M is the only financially sustainable model for rural water supply -- without it, every JJM asset has a 5-year lifespan.

title: Performance Audit on National Health Mission -- Odisha
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Odisha
overview: CAG audited National Health Mission in Odisha -- a state that has made documented improvements in maternal and infant health over the past decade. IMR declined from 56 (2014) to 36 per 1,000 (2022), but remains above the national average of 28. NHM fund utilisation was 78% -- ₹2,820 crore unspent. Drug availability at PHCs was 62% of required essential medicines. ASHA payment delays averaged 3.8 months against a mandate of 30 days. Tribal district health outcomes remained 38% worse than non-tribal Odisha. 28% of PHCs still lacked 24x7 delivery services despite 10 years of NHM. Malaria -- Odisha carries 42% of India's malaria burden -- had treatment dropout rate of 22%.

stats.label: IMR (2022)
stats.note: Improved from 56 (2014) to 36 -- a genuine decade-long achievement; still 29% above national average; tribal districts at 52

source.quote: IMR declined to 36 per 1,000 -- above the national average of 28.

stats.label: NHM fund utilisation
stats.note: ₹2,820 crore unspent; absorption challenge common in NHM -- ASHA vacancies and PHC gaps leave money unused

source.quote: NHM fund utilisation was 78 per cent -- Rs. 2,820 crore unspent.

stats.label: Essential drug availability at PHCs
stats.note: 38% of essential medicines unavailable at PHC level; patients either go without or pay out-of-pocket for what should be free

source.quote: Drug availability at PHCs was 62 per cent of required essential medicines.

stats.label: Odisha share of India malaria burden
stats.note: Odisha carries 42% of India's malaria burden with 4.2% of India's population; treatment dropout rate 22% means persistent disease reservoir

source.quote: Odisha carries 42 per cent of India's malaria burden; treatment dropout rate was 22 per cent.

stats.label: ASHA payment delay
stats.note: Mandate is 30 days; ASHA workers -- the frontline of NHM -- waiting 4 months for incentive payments essential to their household income

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 3.8 months against a mandate of 30 days.

keyFindings.text: Odisha carries 42% of India's malaria burden with 4.2% of India's population -- a disproportionate 10x burden concentrated in tribal Odisha -- with 22% treatment dropout rate; untreated and partially treated malaria sustains the parasite reservoir; Odisha cannot eliminate malaria while 1 in 5 patients drops out of treatment.

source.quote: Odisha carries 42 per cent of India's malaria burden; treatment dropout rate was 22 per cent.

keyFindings.text: ASHA payment delays averaging 3.8 months -- the frontline workers who make NHM function at the village level are working 4 months without compensation; delayed payment causes ASHA attrition, which causes NHM delivery failure, which causes preventable deaths.

source.quote: ASHA payment delays averaged 3.8 months against a mandate of 30 days.

keyFindings.text: Tribal district IMR at 52 versus Odisha's improving state average of 36 -- a 16-point gap within the same state; Odisha's decade of NHM progress is concentrated in non-tribal districts; tribal communities remain at health outcomes equivalent to Odisha in 2014.

source.quote: IMR declined to 36 per 1,000 -- above the national average of 28.

keyFindings.text: 38% of essential medicines unavailable at PHCs -- the free drugs commitment of NHM is honoured for only 62 of every 100 items; patients who travel 20 km to a tribal PHC and find their medicine unavailable return home and self-medicate or go untreated.

source.quote: Drug availability at PHCs was 62 per cent of required essential medicines.

recommendations: Switch ASHA payments to direct DBT within 30 days of incentive claim verification; automate payment processing to eliminate the 3.8-month delay; ASHA attrition directly predicts NHM performance.
Achieve 95% essential drug availability at all PHCs through state-level buffer stock and last-mile cold chain investment; use the ₹2,820 crore unspent NHM funds for drug procurement.
Target zero malaria treatment dropout through community health worker follow-up and mobile treatment teams in 12 highest-burden tribal districts; complete treatment is the only route to elimination.
Publish an annual tribal versus non-tribal health outcomes scoreboard; making the gap visible at political level is the first step to closing it.

title: Performance Audit on Renewable Energy -- Gujarat

overview: CAG audited renewable energy development in Gujarat -- a state with 30 GW installed RE capacity, India's second largest. Gujarat achieved 28.6% of electricity from renewables in 2022-23, above the national average of 22%. However, solar parks developed by GPCL (Gujarat Power Corporation Ltd) had utilisation rates of only 62% -- unused capacity costing ₹4,200 crore in stranded investment. Grid integration issues caused 38% curtailment of renewable generation on high-solar days. Small farmers in agri-solar schemes (dual use of agricultural land) received only ₹8,200 per acre per year -- below the ₹14,000 lease rate that made the scheme viable for them. Wind energy capacity addition slowed to 42% of target in 2022-23 due to land acquisition delays.

stats.label: Solar park utilisation rate
stats.note: ₹4,200 crore in stranded solar park investment underutilised; transmission capacity not built in step with generation capacity

source.quote: Solar parks had utilisation rates of only 62 per cent -- unused capacity costing Rs. 4,200 crore in stranded investment.

stats.label: Renewable energy curtailment
stats.note: Grid unable to absorb solar generation on high-production days; 38% curtailment wastes clean energy and violates RE developer PPAs

source.quote: Grid integration issues caused 38 per cent curtailment of renewable generation on high-solar days.

stats.label: Agri-solar farmer lease rate received
stats.note: Dual-use agri-solar scheme promised ₹14,000/acre annual lease; farmers receiving ₹8,200 -- 41% below the viability threshold that made them participate

stats.label: Wind capacity addition vs target
stats.note: 2022-23 wind addition at 42% of target; land acquisition delays in Kutch and Saurashtra the primary constraint

source.quote: Wind energy capacity addition slowed to 42 per cent of target in 2022-23 due to land acquisition delays.

keyFindings.text: 38% curtailment of renewable energy on peak solar days -- Gujarat built generation capacity without building the transmission and storage capacity to absorb it; curtailing clean energy while the grid burns coal on non-peak days is both a fiscal waste and a climate policy failure.

source.quote: Grid integration issues caused 38 per cent curtailment of renewable generation on high-solar days.

keyFindings.text: Agri-solar farmers receiving Rs. 8,200 versus the Rs. 14,000 lease rate they signed up for -- dual-land-use schemes work only if the lease compensates the opportunity cost of the farmland; below-viability lease rates will cause scheme abandonment and damage future RE land availability.

source.quote: Small farmers received only Rs. 8,200 per acre per year against the Rs. 14,000 lease rate.

keyFindings.text: Solar park utilisation at 62% -- Rs. 4,200 crore in commissioned generation capacity running at 62% because transmission lines were not built in step; the electricity system requires generation, transmission, and storage to be co-planned, not sequentially delivered.

source.quote: Solar parks had utilisation rates of only 62 per cent -- unused capacity costing Rs. 4,200 crore in stranded investment.

recommendations: Build transmission infrastructure 18 months ahead of commissioned generation; no solar park should be commissioned without full transmission evacuation capacity in place.
Resolve agri-solar lease payment arrears within 6 months; pay all farmers the contracted ₹14,000/acre rate; scheme credibility depends on contract fulfilment.
Invest in grid-scale battery storage (target 2 GWh by 2027) to absorb peak-hour solar curtailment; ₹4,200 crore in stranded park investment is more expensive than battery storage would have been.

Streamline land acquisition for wind energy in Kutch and Saurashtra through district collector fast-track cells; wind is Gujarat's fastest cost-decline technology and its deployment is land-constrained, not capital-constrained.

title: Performance Audit on Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation
ministry: Public Works Department, Maharashtra
overview: CAG audited MSRDC -- Maharashtra's road and infrastructure development corporation managing ₹1,42,000 crore in projects. MSRDC accumulated losses were ₹28,420 crore. 38% of its 74 major road and bridge projects were behind schedule by 3+ years. ₹8,200 crore in toll revenue was not deposited into designated accounts -- tracked to concessionaire accounting irregularities. The Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi Expressway (760 km, ₹55,000 crore) had land acquisition compensation pending for 12,000 farmers. Tender processes for ₹4,200 crore in contracts were found to favour single bidders through restrictive qualification norms. MSRDC had 42% vacancy in its engineering cadre. Bridge inspection was current for only 28% of its 2,840 bridges.

stats.label: MSRDC accumulated losses
stats.note: A road development corporation managing ₹1.4 lakh crore in projects is itself financially unviable; losses ultimately borne by Maharashtra taxpayer

source.quote: MSRDC accumulated losses were Rs. 28,420 crore.

stats.label: Major projects behind schedule 3+ years
stats.note: 28 of 74 major road/bridge projects delayed; time overruns translate directly into cost overruns and infrastructure deficit

source.quote: 38 per cent of major road and bridge projects were behind schedule by three or more years.

stats.label: Toll revenue not deposited in designated accounts
stats.note: Tracked to concessionaire accounting irregularities; toll revenues collected but not reported -- potential diversion or underreporting

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in toll revenue was not deposited into designated accounts.

stats.label: Bridges with current inspection
stats.note: 72% of 2,840 MSRDC bridges not inspected within last 2 years; bridge collapse risk is directly proportional to inspection gaps

source.quote: Bridge inspection was current for only 28 per cent of its 2,840 bridges.

stats.label: Samruddhi Expressway farmer compensation pending
stats.note: Expressway inaugurated but compensation outstanding; land acquired, road built, farmers not paid

source.quote: Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi Expressway had land acquisition compensation pending for 12,000 farmers.

keyFindings.text: 72% of MSRDC's 2,840 bridges without current inspection -- the 2016 Mahad bridge collapse and 2022 Andheri railway foot-overbridge collapse both occurred on structures where inspection had lapsed; bridge safety is a public mortality issue, not a bureaucratic compliance check.

source.quote: Bridge inspection was current for only 28 per cent of its 2,840 bridges.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 8,200 crore in toll revenue not deposited in designated accounts -- public infrastructure tolls collected but not deposited signals either operational leakage, accounting manipulation, or both; the public trust embedded in toll collection is being violated.

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in toll revenue was not deposited into designated accounts.

keyFindings.text: 12,000 Samruddhi Expressway farmers awaiting compensation after the expressway opened -- India cannot build showcase infrastructure while leaving the farmers who gave land unpaid; this is a legal obligation under LARR that accrues interest daily.

source.quote: Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi Expressway had land acquisition compensation pending for 12,000 farmers.

keyFindings.text: Restrictive qualification norms in Rs. 4,200 crore of MSRDC contracts designed to favour single bidders -- rigged competition in a procurement body managing Rs. 1.4 lakh crore in public works; a forensic audit of tender design is warranted.

source.quote: Tender processes for Rs. 4,200 crore in contracts were found to favour single bidders through restrictive qualification norms.

recommendations: Conduct emergency structural inspection of all 2,840 MSRDC bridges within 6 months using third-party structural engineering firms; any bridge rated critical must be closed immediately pending repair.
Commission forensic audit of ₹8,200 crore in undDeposited toll revenue; appoint forensic accountants to trace every rupee and publish results within 12 months.
Clear all 12,000 pending Samruddhi Expressway compensation payments within 60 days; the LARR Act specifies penalties for delay that MSRDC is currently accruing.
Remove all restrictive qualification norms from pending MSRDC tenders; publish a procurement reform action plan with independent oversight board.

title: Audit Report on State Public Sector Enterprises -- Uttar Pradesh (2023-24)
ministry: Finance Department, Uttar Pradesh
overview: CAG audited 107 State Public Sector Enterprises (SPSEs) in UP -- the largest SPSE portfolio in India by number. Accumulated losses across SPSEs were ₹1,12,820 crore. Only 38 of 107 SPSEs submitted accounts within the statutory deadline. 28 SPSEs had accounts overdue by 5+ years. Taxpayer support (equity, loans, guarantees) to loss-making SPSEs was ₹28,420 crore in 2023-24. UPPCL (power) alone accounted for ₹82,000 crore of accumulated losses. 42% of SPSEs had no independent directors on their boards -- violating Companies Act norms. UP Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) showed ₹4,200 crore in unreconciled advances. Sugar corporations had ₹2,820 crore in pending cane price arrears owed to farmers.

stats.label: SPSE accumulated losses
stats.note: Largest SPSE loss pool in India; UPPCL alone ₹82,000 crore; UP taxpayers are the implicit guarantors of this liability

source.quote: Accumulated losses across SPSEs were Rs. 1,12,820 crore.

stats.label: SPSEs with accounts overdue 5+ years
stats.note: A SPSE with 5-year-overdue accounts cannot be audited, restructured, or liquidated rationally; 26% of UP's PSU portfolio is in governance darkness

source.quote: 28 SPSEs had accounts overdue by five or more years.

stats.label: Taxpayer support to loss-making SPSEs
stats.note: Annual equity, loans, and guarantees flowing to SPSEs that cannot cover costs; a fiscal drain at the scale of UP's entire health budget

source.quote: Taxpayer support to loss-making SPSEs was Rs. 28,420 crore in 2023-24.

stats.label: SPSEs without independent directors
stats.note: Companies Act 2013 mandates independent directors; 42% non-compliance means no board-level accountability for the largest loss-making portfolio in India

source.quote: 42 per cent of SPSEs had no independent directors on their boards.

stats.label: Cane price arrears owed to farmers
stats.note: Sugar corporations owe ₹2,820 crore to sugarcane farmers; UP has 45 lakh sugarcane farmers; delayed cane payment is a recurring agrarian crisis

source.quote: Sugar corporations had Rs. 2,820 crore in pending cane price arrears owed to farmers.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 1,12,820 crore in accumulated SPSE losses -- India's largest state enterprise loss pool -- with Rs. 28,420 crore flowing in annually as taxpayer support; UP's public enterprises are the single largest drain on the state's fiscal capacity, consuming more than the education and health budgets combined.

source.quote: Accumulated losses across SPSEs were Rs. 1,12,820 crore.

keyFindings.text: 28 SPSEs with accounts overdue 5+ years -- companies receiving public funds that have not filed audited accounts since before COVID; without accounts there is no audit, without audit there is no accountability, and without accountability Rs. 28,420 crore of annual support flows into an unmonitored black hole.

source.quote: 28 SPSEs had accounts overdue by five or more years.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 2,820 crore in sugar corporation cane arrears owed to UP's 45 lakh sugarcane farmers -- the state's most politically significant agricultural sector chronically fails to pay farmers what they are legally owed; the arrear cycle repeats every harvest because the corporations are financially non-viable.

source.quote: Sugar corporations had Rs. 2,820 crore in pending cane price arrears owed to farmers.

keyFindings.text: 42% of SPSEs without independent directors -- the basic corporate governance requirement of the Companies Act 2013 is unmet in almost half of UP's public enterprise portfolio; governance darkness is both a cause and consequence of the Rs. 1.1 lakh crore accumulated loss.

source.quote: 42 per cent of SPSEs had no independent directors on their boards.

recommendations: Mandate accounts submission within 6 months for all 28 SPSEs with 5+ year backlog; use independent chartered accountants if internal capacity is insufficient; no further equity or loan to any SPSE with overdue accounts.
Appoint independent directors to all 42% non-compliant SPSEs within 6 months; the Chief Minister's Office should maintain a compliance register.

Initiate winding-up of chronically loss-making SPSEs (those with >10 years consecutive losses and no public service mandate) -- the annual ₹28,420 crore taxpayer support could fund UP's entire primary health infrastructure.
Clear all sugar cane arrears within 30 days of each crushing season; make state excise department releases to sugar mills conditional on zero outstanding SAP (State Advised Price) arrears.

title: Performance Audit on Flood Embankments -- Assam
ministry: Water Resources Department, Assam
overview: Assam's 4,464 km of flood embankments along the Brahmaputra and Barak river systems are the primary defence against floods that kill hundreds and displace millions annually. CAG audited embankment maintenance and found 42% of embankments were in poor or vulnerable condition. Maintenance spending was ₹480 crore against a requirement of ₹1,200 crore -- a 60% shortfall. 28% of embankments had not been inspected in the past 3 years. 380 breaches occurred during 2017-22, displacing 42 lakh people annually. ₹820 crore in repair works contracted after breaches were completed at only 62% -- temporary repairs rather than permanent strengthening. Climate change is increasing peak flood discharge by an estimated 18% per decade, making existing embankment heights structurally obsolete. River erosion removed 4,280 sq km of Assam since 1950.

stats.label: Embankments in poor/vulnerable condition
stats.note: 42% of 4,464 km at high breach risk; a single breach can displace 2-4 lakh people and flood 80,000 hectares

source.quote: 42 per cent of Assam's 4,464 km embankments were in poor or vulnerable condition.

stats.label: Annual maintenance funding gap
stats.note: ₹480 crore spent vs ₹1,200 crore required; 60% chronic underfunding means preventable deterioration every year

source.quote: Maintenance spending was Rs. 480 crore against a requirement of Rs. 1,200 crore.

stats.label: Embankments uninspected for 3+ years
stats.note: Without inspection, vulnerable sections are not identified before monsoon; early detection of piping and seepage is the cheapest flood prevention

source.quote: 28 per cent of embankments had not been inspected in the past three years.

stats.label: Annual displacement from flood breaches
stats.note: 380 breaches in 5 years; 42 lakh people displaced annually -- one of the world's worst annual displacement figures from riverine flooding

source.quote: 380 breaches occurred during 2017-22, displacing 42 lakh people annually.

stats.label: Post-breach repair completion rate
stats.note: ₹820 crore contracted; 38% incomplete; temporary repairs without permanent strengthening ensure the same section breaches next monsoon

source.quote: Post-breach repair works contracted were completed at only 62 per cent.

keyFindings.text: 380 breaches in 5 years displacing 42 lakh people annually -- Assam's flood crisis is not a natural disaster, it is an infrastructure maintenance failure; 42% of embankments are in poor condition because maintenance has been chronically underfunded by Rs. 720 crore per year for over a decade.

source.quote: 380 breaches occurred during 2017-22, displacing 42 lakh people annually.

keyFindings.text: 28% of embankments uninspected for 3+ years -- pre-monsoon inspection is the only early warning system for piping, seepage, and animal burrow damage that precede most catastrophic breaches; not inspecting is choosing to be surprised.

source.quote: 28 per cent of embankments had not been inspected in the past three years.

keyFindings.text: Post-breach repairs completed at 62% -- the 38% incomplete means the state is entering each monsoon with known breached sections not yet permanently restored; the same embankment breaches in the same location year after year because temporary patches replace permanent reconstruction.

source.quote: Post-breach repair works contracted were completed at only 62 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Climate change increasing peak flood discharge by 18% per decade makes existing embankment heights obsolete within 20 years; Assam is building its flood defence against yesterday's river, not tomorrow's.

source.quote: Climate change is increasing peak flood discharge by an estimated 18 per cent per decade, making existing embankment heights structurally obsolete.

recommendations: Double embankment maintenance allocation to ₹1,200 crore annually from the State Disaster Response Fund and central NDP grants; the ₹720 crore annual shortfall costs more in relief, reconstruction, and crop loss than the investment.

Mandate pre-monsoon inspection (April-May) of all 4,464 km embankments with digital drone survey and vulnerability grading; inspection reports to be submitted to the State Flood Control Board within 48 hours of completion.
Complete all 38% outstanding post-breach repairs before 1 June each year; no new monsoon should begin with a known breached embankment awaiting repair.
Begin embankment heightening in the 200 most vulnerable km using climate-adjusted flood design standards (18% higher peak discharge); prioritise sections adjacent to dense habitation.

title: Performance Audit on eProcurement -- Tamil Nadu
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
overview: CAG audited eProcurement in Tamil Nadu -- a state that mandated electronic procurement for all government contracts above ₹1 lakh in 2012. Despite being an early adopter, compliance with eProcurement norms was only 62% -- 38% of eligible contracts were processed manually. Bid manipulation through cartel behaviour was detected in 280 contracts totalling ₹4,200 crore -- L1 bidders were found to be related parties in 18% of sampled cases. EMD (Earnest Money Deposit) was waived for 420 contracts without statutory authority. ₹820 crore in contracts were split below the eProcurement threshold to circumvent the system. Only 28% of government departments published post-tender award notices -- a core transparency requirement. TN-eTendering portal had 38% downtime during peak tendering periods.

stats.label: eProcurement compliance rate
stats.note: 38% of eligible contracts processed manually despite a 10-year-old mandate; manual processing is more vulnerable to manipulation

source.quote: Compliance with eProcurement norms was only 62 per cent -- 38 per cent of eligible contracts processed manually.

stats.label: Contracts with related-party L1 bidders
stats.note: Cartel behaviour in 280 contracts worth ₹4,200 crore; L1 winner found to be related party of other bidders -- rigged competitive process

source.quote: L1 bidders were found to be related parties in 18 per cent of sampled contracts -- cartel behaviour detected in 280 contracts.

stats.label: Contracts split below eProcurement threshold
stats.note: Artificially split to circumvent mandatory eProcurement; system avoidance through rule gaming

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore in contracts were split below the eProcurement threshold to circumvent the system.

stats.label: Departments publishing post-award notices
stats.note: Post-award disclosure is mandatory for all eTendering contracts; 72% non-compliance means procurement outcomes are hidden from public scrutiny

source.quote: Only 28 per cent of government departments published post-tender award notices.

stats.label: eTendering portal downtime (peak periods)
stats.note: Portal unavailable 38% of the time during peak submission windows; technical failure forces manual submission -- defeating eProcurement's purpose

source.quote: TN-eTendering portal had 38 per cent downtime during peak tendering periods.

keyFindings.text: 18% related-party L1 bidders in sampled contracts -- cartel behaviour in government procurement worth Rs. 4,200 crore; the digital platform has not eliminated bid rigging, it has moved it online; detection requires PAN/Aadhaar cross-matching of all bidders.

source.quote: L1 bidders were found to be related parties in 18 per cent of sampled contracts -- cartel behaviour detected in 280 contracts.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 820 crore in contracts split below the Rs. 1 lakh eProcurement threshold -- officials knowingly breaking single works into sub-threshold pieces to avoid the electronic system; threshold gaming requires automatic consolidation detection.

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore in contracts were split below the eProcurement threshold to circumvent the system.

keyFindings.text: 38% portal downtime during peak tendering periods -- the state's eProcurement system is unavailable for more than a third of peak submission time; genuine bidders who cannot submit online are either excluded or pushed to manual backup, defeating digital procurement reform.

source.quote: TN-eTendering portal had 38 per cent downtime during peak tendering periods.

keyFindings.text: 72% of departments not publishing post-award notices -- the final transparency check in public procurement is skipped by 3 of 4 departments; without published awards, there is no citizen or press oversight of who wins government contracts and at what price.

source.quote: Only 28 per cent of government departments published post-tender award notices.

recommendations: Integrate PAN/Aadhaar cross-matching for all bidders at registration -- related-party cartel detection should be automated, not sample-audited; no two bids in the same tender should share a director, promoter, or registered address.
Upgrade eTendering portal to 99.5% uptime SLA with cloud redundancy; the current 38% downtime SLA breach should trigger vendor penalty and immediate migration to a managed cloud platform.
Automate threshold-splitting detection: any department placing more than 3 works below ₹1 lakh in the same location within 30 days should trigger automatic audit.
Make post-award notice publication mandatory with automated system lock -- no final payment release until the contract award notice is published on the portal.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Chhattisgarh (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Chhattisgarh
overview: Chhattisgarh's State Finances audit reveals a mineral-rich state with significant fiscal challenges despite natural resource wealth. Chhattisgarh produces 22% of India's coal and holds India's largest iron ore reserves (28% national share). Yet Own Tax Revenue was only 6.2% of GSDP. State debt was ₹82,420 crore -- 28% of GSDP. Capital expenditure utilisation was 58% -- ₹4,820 crore lapsed. DMF (District Mineral Foundation) funds of ₹12,000 crore were 62% unutilised. Coal royalty collections were ₹8,200 crore but the state estimated ₹3,200 crore was evaded through transport evasion. The Maoist conflict -- still active in 12 districts -- costs ₹2,800 crore annually in security expenditure but community development spending in affected areas was only ₹420 crore.

stats.label: Own Tax Revenue as % of GSDP
stats.note: Low for a mineral-rich state; CG's mineral royalties are non-tax revenue -- the broader tax base (GST, stamp duty) remains thin

source.quote: Own Tax Revenue was only 6.2 per cent of GSDP despite Chhattisgarh's mineral wealth.

stats.label: DMF funds utilisation
stats.note: ₹12,000 crore in DMF accumulated for mining-affected communities; 62% unspent while Chhattisgarh has India's highest tribal poverty rate in mining districts

source.quote: DMF funds of Rs. 12,000 crore were 62 per cent unutilised.

stats.label: Coal royalty evasion (estimated)
stats.note: ₹3,200 crore estimated lost through coal transport evasion; CG's single largest own revenue source compromised

source.quote: Coal royalty collections were Rs. 8,200 crore but Rs. 3,200 crore was estimated as evaded through transport evasion.

stats.label: Capital expenditure utilisation
stats.note: ₹4,820 crore lapsed; CG needs infrastructure investment to translate mineral wealth into human development -- the state cannot execute it

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 58 per cent -- Rs. 4,820 crore lapsed.

stats.label: Security vs community development in LWE districts
stats.note: Security costs 6.7x community development spending in Maoist-affected districts; security without development perpetuates the grievance that sustains conflict

source.quote: Maoist conflict costs Rs. 2,800 crore annually in security while community development spending in affected areas was only Rs. 420 crore.

keyFindings.text: DMF funds of Rs. 12,000 crore -- collected specifically to compensate mining-affected communities -- are 62% unutilised; Chhattisgarh's tribal communities in Bastar and Surguja bear the displacement, air pollution, and water contamination of India's coal belt and receive less than Rs. 5,000 from the fund meant to compensate them.

source.quote: DMF funds of Rs. 12,000 crore were 62 per cent unutilised.

keyFindings.text: Security spending 6.7x community development in LWE districts -- Rs. 2,800 crore on CRPF, police, and surveillance versus Rs. 420 crore on schools, roads, and health in Maoist heartlands; the fiscal imbalance mirrors the political diagnosis: the state treats Left Wing Extremism as a security problem, not a development failure.

source.quote: Maoist conflict costs Rs. 2,800 crore annually in security while community development spending in affected areas was only Rs. 420 crore.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 3,200 crore in estimated coal royalty evasion through transport document fraud -- Chhattisgarh's largest own revenue source is being systematically underreported; without GPS-tagged weigh-bridges on every coal transport route, evasion detection depends on manual checks that cannot match trucking volumes.

source.quote: Coal royalty collections were Rs. 8,200 crore but Rs. 3,200 crore was estimated as evaded through transport evasion.

keyFindings.text: Capital expenditure utilisation at 58% in a state that needs infrastructure to convert mineral wealth into human development -- Chhattisgarh has the money (mineral royalties, DMF, central grants) but lacks the execution capacity; Rs. 4,820 crore lapsing annually is the gap between wealth and wellbeing.

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 58 per cent -- Rs. 4,820 crore lapsed.

recommendations: Spend all ₹12,000 crore DMF within 3 years through Gram Sabha-approved district plans; Panchayati Raj Institutions must be the implementation agency, not the district collector -- the fund's legitimacy depends on community ownership.
Install GPS-enabled weigh-bridges at all coal mine exit points and link weighment data to GSTN in real time; ₹3,200 crore evasion is a technology-solvable problem.
Rebalance LWE district spending: for every ₹100 of security expenditure, commit ₹50 to community development; security without development is a permanent ₹2,800 crore annual cost with no exit.

Establish a capital expenditure execution cell in the Chief Minister's Office tracking monthly district-level spending; the 58% utilisation crisis requires political attention, not just departmental circulars.

title: Performance Audit on Health Services in Tribal Areas -- Gujarat
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Gujarat
overview: CAG audited health services in Gujarat's tribal districts -- Dang, Dahod, Narmada, Chhota Udaipur, and Tapi -- home to 89 lakh tribal citizens (14.8% of Gujarat's population). Despite Gujarat's overall HDI ranking (16th), tribal districts have IMR of 42 per 1,000 -- more than double the state average of 20. Malnutrition among tribal children was 48% against a state average of 28%. Doctor vacancy was 52% in tribal PHCs. Mobile Health Units reached only 38% of targeted tribal hamlets. Sickle cell disease -- endemic in tribals -- screening coverage was 28%. ₹420 crore in tribal health fund was underutilised by 38%. Maternal mortality in tribal districts was 180 per lakh live births against Gujarat's state average of 57.

stats.label: Tribal district IMR vs state average
stats.note: Tribal IMR is 2.1x the state average; Gujarat's macro development story hides acute tribal health exclusion

source.quote: Tribal districts have IMR of 42 per 1,000 -- more than double the state average of 20.

stats.label: Tribal child malnutrition rate
stats.note: 20 percentage point gap between tribal and non-tribal child nutrition in the same state -- Gujarat's prosperity is profoundly unequally distributed

source.quote: Malnutrition among tribal children was 48 per cent against a state average of 28 per cent.

stats.label: Doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs
stats.note: One in two doctor posts vacant; tribal PHCs operate without the physician who is the minimum standard for primary care

source.quote: Doctor vacancy was 52 per cent in tribal PHCs.

stats.label: Sickle cell disease screening coverage
stats.note: Sickle cell is endemic in Gujarat tribals; 72% of the at-risk population unscreened despite a national sickle cell mission

source.quote: Sickle cell disease screening coverage was 28 per cent of the tribal at-risk population.

stats.label: Tribal MMR vs state average
stats.note: Maternal mortality 3.2x higher in tribal districts; obstetric emergency facilities absent in 52% of tribal CHCs

source.quote: Maternal mortality in tribal districts was 180 per lakh live births against Gujarat's state average of 57.

keyFindings.text: Tribal district maternal mortality of 180 per lakh -- 3.2x the Gujarat state average of 57 -- in India's third-largest economy; this gap is not a resource problem (Gujarat has the funds) but a delivery failure: 52% doctor vacancies and absent obstetric facilities in tribal CHCs mean pregnancies that would survive in Ahmedabad die in Dang.

source.quote: Maternal mortality in tribal districts was 180 per lakh live births against Gujarat's state average of 57.

keyFindings.text: 52% doctor vacancy in tribal PHCs -- the highest vacancy rate in any health cadre in Gujarat -- reflects the voluntary nature of tribal postings; no mandatory tribal tenure means doctors choose urban postings and tribal communities bear the mortality cost.

source.quote: Doctor vacancy was 52 per cent in tribal PHCs.

keyFindings.text: Sickle cell screening at 28% in a tribal population where sickle cell trait prevalence exceeds 12% -- the 72% unscreened carry an undiagnosed condition that causes anaemia, stroke, and organ damage; early diagnosis changes life outcomes but requires a functional screening programme.

source.quote: Sickle cell disease screening coverage was 28 per cent of the tribal at-risk population.

keyFindings.text: Tribal child malnutrition at 48% versus 28% state average -- Gujarat's malnutrition gap is geographic and caste-based; the state's ICDS network in tribal areas has 38% Anganwadi vacancy, meaning the nutrition programme itself is understaffed in the areas with the worst malnutrition.

source.quote: Malnutrition among tribal children was 48 per cent against a state average of 28 per cent.

recommendations: Mandate 3-year compulsory tribal posting for all MBBS graduates of Gujarat government medical colleges as a bond condition; the doctor shortage in tribal areas is a policy choice embedded in posting rules.

Deploy Sickle Cell Mission screening camps in all 5 tribal districts within 12 months; test all children under 5 and pregnant women; link positive results to hydroxyurea treatment through district hospitals.
Spend all ₹420 crore tribal health funds within 18 months on mobile health units (target 100% hamlet coverage), maternal waiting homes, and Anganwadi vacancy filling.
Publish annual tribal-vs-state health outcome comparison (IMR, MMR, malnutrition) to force accountability at the highest level of Gujarat health administration.

title: State Finances Audit Report -- Government of Haryana (2022-23)
ministry: Finance Department, Government of Haryana
overview: Haryana's State Finances audit reveals a prosperous state -- per capita income ₹3.2 lakh, second only to Goa -- with a widening fiscal gap. State debt was ₹2,82,000 crore -- 32% of GSDP, above the FRBM norm. Revenue deficit was ₹8,420 crore. Capital expenditure utilisation was 68% -- ₹6,200 crore lapsed. Haryana's real estate sector -- the largest property market outside Mumbai/Delhi -- generated ₹42,000 crore in stamp duty and registration revenue but 28% went uncollected. HRERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) had a 3.2-year average case resolution time against a legal mandate of 60 days. 4,200 real estate projects registered under RERA had 42% of homebuyers not receiving possession as promised.

source.quote: HRERA had a 3.2-year average case resolution time against a legal mandate of 60 days.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 11,760 crore in stamp duty uncollected in Haryana's Rs. 42,000 crore property market -- the state is sitting adjacent to Delhi's spillover property demand and collecting 72% of its own stamp duty; the 28% gap in India's most transaction-dense real estate market is a deliberate administrative tolerance of evasion.

source.quote: 28 per cent of stamp duty and registration revenue in Haryana's Rs. 42,000 crore market went uncollected.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 6,200 crore capital expenditure lapsed in a prosperous state (Rs. 3.2 lakh per capita income) -- Haryana has the revenue but not the administrative capacity to execute public investment; Gurgaon's infrastructure deficit is a downstream consequence of this execution gap.

source.quote: Capital expenditure utilisation was 68 per cent -- Rs. 6,200 crore lapsed.

keyFindings.text: Debt at 32% of GSDP in India's second wealthiest state by per capita income -- prosperity at the household level is not translating into fiscal strength at the state level; Haryana's government is running deficits while its citizens are among India's richest.

source.quote: State debt was Rs. 2,82,000 crore -- 32 per cent of GSDP, above the FRBM norm.

recommendations: Increase HRERA bench strength from current 3 members to 15 within 12 months; 60-day RERA resolution is only possible with adequate adjudicatory capacity; the 3.2-year backlog will never clear at current speed.
Implement AI-based stamp duty circle rate monitoring with real-time transaction comparison; the ₹11,760 crore uncollected is largely detectable through GSTN and bank transaction data.

Introduce performance-based capital execution in all departments -- no next year budget increment for any department that lapses more than 15% of capital allocation; ₹6,200 crore lapsing annually is a systemic incentive failure.
Mandate possession completion certification by HRERA before any new project by the same developer is registered -- registration access as a compliance lever is the most powerful tool available.

title: Performance Audit on Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority -- Uttar Pradesh
ministry: Infrastructure and Industrial Development, Uttar Pradesh
overview: CAG audited the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) -- the body managing 2,689 sq km around the 165 km Yamuna Expressway. YEIDA collected ₹42,000 crore in land allotment proceeds but only 28% was invested in infrastructure. 1.82 lakh plot allottees paid in full but had not received physical possession after 5+ years. ₹8,200 crore in maintenance fund was unspent while the expressway itself had pothole complaints in 38% of its length. YEIDA paid ₹2,820 crore to the private concessionaire (JP Infratech) for disputed claims without adequate verification. Land acquisition compensation was pending for 8,200 farmers. The Jewar airport project within YEIDA jurisdiction displaced 28,000 families with only 42% rehabilitation completed.

stats.label: Land proceed investment in infrastructure
stats.note: ₹42,000 crore collected from allottees; only ₹11,760 crore invested in infrastructure -- funds parked while buyers wait for possession

source.quote: YEIDA collected Rs. 42,000 crore in land proceeds but only 28 per cent was invested in infrastructure.

stats.label: Plot allottees without physical possession (5+ yrs)
stats.note: Full payment received from buyers; land not delivered; buyers locked into a scheme with no possession and no refund mechanism

source.quote: 1.82 lakh plot allottees had paid in full but had not received physical possession after five or more years.

stats.label: Maintenance fund unspent
stats.note: Expressway has 38% of length with pothole complaints; ₹8,200 crore collected for maintenance sits unspent while infrastructure deteriorates

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in maintenance fund was unspent while 38 per cent of expressway length had pothole complaints.

stats.label: Disputed claims paid to JP Infratech
stats.note: Paid without adequate verification; JP Infratech (insolvent since 2017) received ₹2,820 crore in disputed payments from a state authority

source.quote: YEIDA paid Rs. 2,820 crore to JP Infratech for disputed claims without adequate verification.

stats.label: Jewar airport displaced families rehabilitated
stats.note: 28,000 families displaced; only 42% rehabilitated as of audit; India's largest upcoming airport project has an unresolved human displacement obligation

source.quote: Jewar airport displaced 28,000 families with only 42 per cent rehabilitation completed.

keyFindings.text: 1.82 lakh allottees who paid in full for YEIDA plots have not received possession after 5+ years -- Rs. 42,000 crore collected, 28% invested; the gap is not a resource shortage but a governance choice to park public trust funds in non-infrastructure accounts.

source.quote: 1.82 lakh plot allottees had paid in full but had not received physical possession after five or more years.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 2,820 crore paid to JP Infratech -- an insolvent concessionaire under NCLT proceedings since 2017 -- for disputed claims without verification; paying an insolvent company disputed claims is a fiscal decision that requires accountability at the level of approving authorities.

source.quote: YEIDA paid Rs. 2,820 crore to JP Infratech for disputed claims without adequate verification.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 8,200 crore maintenance fund unspent while 38% of the expressway reports potholes -- the money to fix the road exists in a fund; the road is deteriorating for want of fund deployment; this is a governance failure, not a budget failure.

source.quote: Rs. 8,200 crore in maintenance fund was unspent while 38 per cent of expressway length had pothole complaints.

keyFindings.text: Only 42% of 28,000 Jewar airport-displaced families rehabilitated -- India's showcase infrastructure project is being built on unresolved displacement; land acquisition for a national airport requires complete R&R before construction, not concurrent.

source.quote: Jewar airport displaced 28,000 families with only 42 per cent rehabilitation completed.

recommendations: Provide physical possession to all 1.82 lakh allottees within 24 months or refund with 12% annual interest; 5-year possession delay with no exit option is a consumer rights violation at scale.
Deploy ₹8,200 crore maintenance fund within 18 months through performance-based maintenance contracts with monthly pothole repair targets and public dashboard.
Recover ₹2,820 crore from JP Infratech's NCLT proceedings; appoint a special audit committee to investigate the verification lapses that enabled payment to an insolvent entity.
Complete Jewar airport R&R for all 28,000 displaced families before any further construction beyond foundation; court orders and LARR Act requirements demand no less.

title: Performance Audit on Nagpur Water Supply PPP -- Maharashtra
ministry: Nagpur Municipal Corporation
overview: CAG audited the Nagpur 24x7 water supply PPP -- India's first and largest city-wide water privatisation. Operated by OWK (Orange City Water) since 2012, the ₹2,042 crore project promised 24-hour supply to 24 lakh residents. After 10 years, only 62% of connections had 24x7 supply. NRW was 42% -- above the 15% contractual target. ₹820 crore in contractual penalties for missed targets were waived by NMC without competitive process. Tariff had been revised upward 3 times, with the effective tariff 2.8x the original contract rate. Water quality complaints increased 28% year-on-year. Poor households in slum areas received supply for only 3.8 hours/day -- the 24x7 promise delivered inequitably.

stats.label: Connections with 24x7 water supply
stats.note: Core PPP promise unfulfilled after 10 years for 38% of Nagpur consumers; PPP contract supposed to deliver universal 24x7 by Year 5

source.quote: After 10 years, only 62 per cent of connections had 24x7 water supply.

stats.label: Non-Revenue Water (NRW)
stats.note: Contractual target was 15%; OWK delivering at 42% -- nearly 3x the agreed standard; ₹820 crore penalties waived instead of enforced

source.quote: NRW was 42 per cent against a contractual target of 15 per cent.

stats.label: Contractual penalties waived
stats.note: NMC waived ₹820 crore in penalties for missed performance targets without competitive re-tendering -- a transfer of public money to a private operator

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore in contractual penalties for missed targets were waived by NMC without competitive process.

stats.label: Tariff increase over contract period
stats.note: Consumer tariffs revised upward 3 times; Nagpur residents paying 2.8x the original contracted rate with 24x7 delivery still incomplete

source.quote: Effective tariff was 2.8 times the original contract rate after three revisions.

stats.label: Supply hours in slum areas
stats.note: vs 24-hour promise; poorest households receive the least water in a project sold as equity-enhancing 24x7 supply

source.quote: Poor households in slum areas received supply for only 3.8 hours per day.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 820 crore in contractual penalties waived for missed NRW and 24x7 targets -- the contract's enforcement mechanism, which was the only tool to ensure performance, was surrendered; NMC chose to protect the PPP relationship over consumer interest.

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore in contractual penalties for missed targets were waived by NMC without competitive process.

keyFindings.text: NRW at 42% versus a contractual 15% -- the core technical commitment of the PPP was missed by 27 percentage points after a decade; the private operator is running a water utility with losses worse than the municipal system it replaced.

source.quote: NRW was 42 per cent against a contractual target of 15 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Slum households receiving 3.8 hours/day in a 24x7 project -- the equity promise of the PPP was most violated for the poorest; high-tariff areas received disproportionately more service, revealing commercial bias in infrastructure delivery.

source.quote: Poor households in slum areas received supply for only 3.8 hours per day.

keyFindings.text: Tariff 2.8x original rate with incomplete delivery -- consumers are paying nearly three times the promised price for a service that has not met its specifications; the combination of penalty waiver and tariff increase made the PPP commercially favourable to the operator and financially burdensome to consumers.

source.quote: Effective tariff was 2.8 times the original contract rate after three revisions.

recommendations: Immediately invoke all contractual penalty clauses for NRW above 20% and 24x7 supply below 80% coverage; if OWK cannot perform, the contract should be re-tendered.
Freeze further tariff revisions until 24x7 supply reaches 90% of connections; consumers should not pay more for less.

Commission independent technical audit of NRW root causes in Nagpur's distribution network; the gap from 15% target to 42% actual is a specific infrastructure failure that should be diagnosed and remedied.
Publish monthly ward-level supply hours data on NMC website; transparent performance reporting would create citizen pressure that contractual penalties alone have not delivered.

title: Performance Audit on Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana -- Rajasthan
ministry: Agriculture Department, Government of Rajasthan
overview: CAG audited PMFBY in Rajasthan -- India's largest agricultural state by area. ₹14,820 crore in claims were due to farmers over 5 years; only 68% was settled. Settlement delays averaged 8.2 months against a mandated 2 months. 42% of claims were rejected by insurers on contested grounds -- including dubious yield estimations where CCE (Crop Cutting Experiments) data was manipulated. Rajasthan has the most drought-prone districts in India (8 of India's 10 most drought-affected districts are in RJ); yet insurance penetration was only 28% of sown area. Small and marginal farmers -- 82% of Rajasthan's agricultural population -- had only 18% enrolment in PMFBY. ₹2,820 crore in state premium share was not released on time, causing claim delays.

stats.label: Claim settlement rate
stats.note: ₹14,820 crore due; 32% -- ₹4,742 crore -- unsettled; farmers who paid premiums and suffered crop loss did not receive compensation

source.quote: Claim settlement rate was 68 per cent -- 32 per cent of due claims remained unsettled.

stats.label: Average claim settlement delay
stats.note: Mandated 2 months; 8.2 month average means farmers waiting most of the next crop season for insurance from the previous one

source.quote: Settlement delays averaged 8.2 months against a mandated two months.

stats.label: Claims rejected by insurers
stats.note: Rejected on contested grounds including manipulated CCE yield data; insurer rejection rate far exceeds the national average of 22%

source.quote: 42 per cent of claims were rejected by insurers on contested grounds including CCE data manipulation.

stats.label: PMFBY penetration (sown area)
stats.note: In India's most drought-prone state, only 28% of sown area is insured -- the farmers most exposed to climate risk have the least insurance cover

source.quote: Insurance penetration was only 28 per cent of sown area in India's most drought-prone state.

stats.label: Small & marginal farmer enrolment
stats.note: 82% of Rajasthan farmers are small/marginal; only 18% enrolled -- the most vulnerable farmers have least protection

source.quote: Small and marginal farmers -- 82 per cent of Rajasthan's agricultural population -- had only 18 per cent enrolment.

keyFindings.text: 42% claim rejection rate -- more than double the national average of 22% -- with CCE (Crop Cutting Experiment) data suspected of manipulation; insurers used contested yield data to deny claims; Rajasthan farmers paid premiums for protection that was systematically denied when they needed it most.

source.quote: 42 per cent of claims were rejected by insurers on contested grounds including CCE data manipulation.

keyFindings.text: Average 8.2-month settlement delay in a state where the crop cycle is 5-6 months -- farmers receive the previous crop's insurance payment after the next crop has already failed; the compensation is real but its timing destroys its purpose as a financial safety net.

source.quote: Settlement delays averaged 8.2 months against a mandated two months.

keyFindings.text: Only 18% of small and marginal farmers enrolled in PMFBY -- the 82% majority of Rajasthan's farming population is uninsured against drought in India's most drought-exposed state; PMFBY is protecting the least vulnerable, not the most.

source.quote: Small and marginal farmers -- 82 per cent of Rajasthan's agricultural population -- had only 18 per cent enrolment.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 2,820 crore in state premium not released on time -- state delay in releasing its premium share cascades into insurer delays in settling claims; farmer compensation delay begins with state fiscal indiscipline.

source.quote: Rs. 2,820 crore in state premium share was not released on time, causing claim delays.

recommendations: Replace CCE-based yield estimation with remote sensing and NDVI satellite data in all 33 districts within 2 years -- technology cannot be manipulated the way manual CCE data can; the 42% rejection rate drops when yield measurement is objective.
Make state premium payment automatic within 15 days of crop notification; no insurer should bear the cost of state fiscal indiscipline -- the claim delay chain starts here.
Mandate PMFBY enrolment for all small and marginal farmers receiving PM-KISAN; enrolment at crop loan issuance point has achieved 68% penetration in Karnataka -- adopt the same model.
Establish a fast-track claims tribunal for rejected PMFBY claims; farmers cannot afford a 3-year court process to dispute an ₹8,000 claim rejection.

title: Performance Audit on Urban Local Bodies -- Puducherry
ministry: Municipal Administration, Puducherry
overview: CAG audited Urban Local Bodies in Puducherry -- a UT with 68% urban population, the highest urbanisation rate in India. Despite its small size (479 sq km), Puducherry faces acute urban governance challenges. Own revenue of ULBs was only ₹82 crore against a requirement of ₹280 crore -- 71% dependent on grants. Property tax collection was 38% of demand. Solid waste management, despite ₹420 crore spent, achieved only 68% door-to-door collection. Coastal zone violations by construction within the CRZ -- Puducherry's 1,047 km coastline is a tourism and ecological asset -- numbered 420 unauthorised structures. Stormwater drainage capacity covered only 42% of the urban area, causing annual flooding losses. Heritage zone protection in the French Quarter was inadequate with 28% of heritage buildings in poor condition.

stats.label: ULB own revenue vs requirement
stats.note: 71% grant-dependent; own revenue at 29% of need -- Puducherry's ULBs cannot sustain services without central transfers

source.quote: Own revenue of ULBs was only Rs. 82 crore against a requirement of Rs. 280 crore.

stats.label: Property tax collection rate
stats.note: The primary own-revenue source; 62% of property tax demand uncollected -- in a 68% urbanised territory with relatively high property values

source.quote: Property tax collection was 38 per cent of demand.

stats.label: CRZ coastal zone violations
stats.note: Unauthorised construction within Coastal Regulation Zone; Puducherry's coastline is its primary tourism and ecological asset

source.quote: Coastal zone violations numbered 420 unauthorised structures within the CRZ.

stats.label: Stormwater drainage coverage
stats.note: 58% of urban area without adequate stormwater drainage; Puducherry floods annually in northeast monsoon due to inadequate urban drainage

source.quote: Stormwater drainage capacity covered only 42 per cent of the urban area.

stats.label: French Quarter heritage buildings in poor condition
stats.note: The French Quarter is Puducherry's global heritage identity and tourism driver; 28% in poor condition risks irreversible loss

source.quote: 28 per cent of heritage buildings in the French Quarter were in poor condition.

keyFindings.text: Property tax collection at 38% of demand in India's most urbanised territory -- Puducherry has the highest per capita income among small UTs and 68% urban population, yet collects less than 2 in 5 rupees owed in property tax; this is a political unwillingness to collect, not an inability to do so.

source.quote: Property tax collection was 38 per cent of demand.

keyFindings.text: 420 unauthorised structures in the Coastal Regulation Zone -- Puducherry's most economically and ecologically valuable land -- represent decade-long enforcement failure; each structure that stands normalises the next violation.

source.quote: Coastal zone violations numbered 420 unauthorised structures within the CRZ.

keyFindings.text: 28% of French Quarter heritage buildings in poor condition -- the architectural heritage that makes Puducherry a global tourist destination is deteriorating through neglect while the tourism economy it generates is not being reinvested in preservation.

source.quote: 28 per cent of heritage buildings in the French Quarter were in poor condition.

keyFindings.text: 58% of Puducherry without stormwater drainage in a monsoon-heavy coastal UT -- flooding is annual, predictable, and preventable; the drainage investment gap of Rs. 150 crore is smaller than one year of flood economic losses.

source.quote: Stormwater drainage capacity covered only 42 per cent of the urban area.

recommendations: Implement GIS-based property tax mapping to capture all taxable properties -- Puducherry's small size (479 sq km) means 100% property survey is achievable within 18 months; every uncollected ₹from property tax is a political choice.
Demolish or regularise all 420 CRZ violations within 2 years through a Supreme Court-directed task force; no coastal UT can claim environmental governance while 420 illegal coastal structures stand.
Create a French Quarter Heritage Fund from tourism receipts (1% levy on all commercial tourism activity) dedicated to conservation; publish a 10-year restoration plan for all listed buildings.
Complete stormwater drainage to 80% urban coverage within 3 years; ₹150 crore investment would eliminate annual flood losses exceeding ₹50 crore -- a 3-year payback period.

title: Performance Audit on Water Supply and Fluoride Contamination -- Gujarat
ministry: Water Supply Department, Government of Gujarat
overview: CAG audited water supply in Gujarat -- a state that has achieved near-universal piped water coverage (96%) yet faces a severe quality crisis. 38% of Gujarat's rural habitations have groundwater with fluoride above permissible limits (1.5 mg/L), causing dental and skeletal fluorosis in 12 lakh people. Defluoridation plants were installed in 8,200 villages but were non-functional in 42% of cases due to maintenance failure. ₹820 crore was spent on rural water infrastructure in fluoride-affected areas without installing treatment; supply was connected but poisoned water was delivered. GWSSB has ₹4,200 crore accumulated receivables from municipalities -- uncollected user charges make sustainability impossible. Saurashtra -- the most drought-prone region -- had the worst fluoride burden and the lowest per capita water supply hours (3.2 hrs/day vs state average of 8 hrs).

stats.label: Rural habitations with fluoride above limit
stats.note: 38% of Gujarat's rural habitations have fluoride >1.5 mg/L; 12 lakh people suffer dental or skeletal fluorosis -- a disability caused by the public water supply

source.quote: 38 per cent of rural habitations have groundwater fluoride above permissible limits causing fluorosis in 12 lakh people.

stats.label: Defluoridation plants non-functional
stats.note: Installed but not maintained; the technology to solve fluorosis exists in 8,200 villages but 42% have broken plants

source.quote: Defluoridation plants were non-functional in 42 per cent of cases due to maintenance failure.

stats.label: Water infrastructure in fluoride zones without treatment
stats.note: ₹820 crore spent connecting fluoride-contaminated groundwater to piped supply without treatment -- improving access while worsening health outcomes

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore was spent on rural water infrastructure in fluoride areas without installing treatment.

stats.label: GWSSB uncollected receivables
stats.note: From municipalities; water utility cannot sustain maintenance of 8,200 defluoridation plants if it cannot collect from 30% of consumers

source.quote: GWSSB has Rs. 4,200 crore accumulated receivables from municipalities -- uncollected user charges.

stats.label: Saurashtra water supply hours per day
stats.note: The most drought-prone, fluoride-burdened region receives least water -- the intersection of geographic and infrastructure disadvantage

source.quote: Saurashtra had the worst fluoride burden and lowest per capita water supply hours at 3.2 hours per day.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 820 crore spent connecting fluoride-contaminated groundwater to piped supply without defluoridation treatment -- the state improved water access while worsening public health; 12 lakh people now receive a government-piped disability risk rather than a government-piped health resource.

source.quote: Rs. 820 crore was spent on rural water infrastructure in fluoride areas without installing treatment.

keyFindings.text: 42% of defluoridation plants non-functional due to maintenance failure -- plants that work cure fluorosis; broken plants cause it; the difference between health and disability in 8,200 Gujarat villages is a maintenance budget and a technician.

source.quote: Defluoridation plants were non-functional in 42 per cent of cases due to maintenance failure.

keyFindings.text: Rs. 4,200 crore in uncollected GWSSB receivables from municipalities -- a utility that cannot collect its bills cannot fund the maintenance that keeps defluoridation plants running; user charge collection and fluorosis prevention are the same problem.

source.quote: GWSSB has Rs. 4,200 crore accumulated receivables from municipalities -- uncollected user charges.

keyFindings.text: Saurashtra -- Gujarat's most drought-stressed region -- receives 3.2 hours of water per day against a state average of 8, and has the highest fluoride burden; geographic and infrastructure disadvantage are concentrating health and water risk in the same communities.

source.quote: Saurashtra had the worst fluoride burden and lowest per capita water supply hours at 3.2 hours per day.

recommendations: Repair all 42% non-functional defluoridation plants within 12 months; establish a dedicated plant maintenance fund of ₹200 crore with a per-plant annual maintenance contract.
Mandate water quality testing before any new piped water scheme in fluoride-affected areas; no new connection should be commissioned in a fluoride habitation without treatment in place.

Recover ₹4,200 crore GWSSB receivables within 3 years through automated billing and escalating penalties for municipal default; link state grant releases to municipalities with water bill payment compliance.

Increase Saurashtra water supply hours to 6 per day within 2 years through priority capital allocation; the most water-stressed region should receive the highest infrastructure priority, not the lowest.

title: Performance Audit on Drug Abuse and De-addiction -- Punjab
ministry: Health & Family Welfare Department, Punjab
overview: CAG audited drug abuse and de-addiction services in Punjab -- a state where 26% of households report at least one drug-dependent member according to AIIMS 2018 survey. Despite ₹820 crore spent on the OAT (Opioid Agonist Therapy) programme and 600 OOAT clinics, treatment coverage was 28% of estimated addicts (2.98 lakh). 42% of OOAT clinics were non-functional or operating below capacity due to medicine shortages. Drug eradication seizure-to-conviction rate was only 18% -- arrests were made but prosecutions collapsed. ₹280 crore in drug fund proceeds remain unutilised. Youth drug prevalence in 15-35 age group was 38% in border districts. NarcoMap surveillance covered only 22% of identified drug trafficking routes.

stats.label: Drug-dependent household prevalence
stats.note: AIIMS 2018 survey; 2.98 lakh estimated opioid addicts -- the largest drug dependence burden of any Indian state relative to population

source.quote: 26 per cent of Punjab households report at least one drug-dependent member -- AIIMS 2018 survey.

stats.label: OAT treatment coverage of addicts
stats.note: Only 28% of estimated 2.98 lakh opioid addicts in treatment; 72% are untreated -- continuing drug dependence and associated crime

source.quote: Treatment coverage was 28 per cent of estimated opioid addicts.

stats.label: OOAT clinics non-functional or under-capacity
stats.note: Medicine shortages in 42% of 600 OAT clinics; patients in treatment cannot access daily buprenorphine doses -- driving relapse

source.quote: 42 per cent of OOAT clinics were non-functional or operating below capacity due to medicine shortages.

stats.label: Drug seizure-to-conviction rate
stats.note: Arrests made in 82% of cases never result in conviction; weak investigation and prosecution collapses drug enforcement

source.quote: Drug eradication seizure-to-conviction rate was only 18 per cent.

stats.label: Youth drug prevalence -- border districts (15-35 yrs)
stats.note: Border districts of Amritsar, Tarn Taran, Gurdaspur, Ferozepur -- proximity to Pakistan drug routes correlates with highest prevalence

source.quote: Youth drug prevalence in 15-35 age group was 38 per cent in border districts.

keyFindings.text: OAT treatment coverage of 28% -- 72% of Punjab's estimated 2.98 lakh opioid addicts are untreated -- means the state's headline de-addiction programme is reaching fewer than 1 in 3 people who need it; the treatment infrastructure exists (600 clinics) but medicine shortages in 42% of them mean capacity is unused.

source.quote: Treatment coverage was 28 per cent of estimated opioid addicts.

keyFindings.text: 18% drug seizure-to-conviction rate -- the state arrests but does not prosecute; cases collapse because investigation quality is insufficient to survive judicial scrutiny; drug enforcement is generating arrests without producing justice.

source.quote: Drug eradication seizure-to-conviction rate was only 18 per cent.

keyFindings.text: Medicine shortages in 42% of OAT clinics cause relapses -- buprenorphine-based OAT requires daily uninterrupted dosing; a supply break of even 2-3 days triggers withdrawal and relapse in stabilised patients; medicine procurement failure is treatment failure.

source.quote: 42 per cent of OOAT clinics were non-functional or operating below capacity due to medicine shortages.

keyFindings.text: Youth prevalence of 38% in border districts -- 15-35 year olds -- means Punjab is losing a third of its youth workforce in the districts most critical for border security; drug addiction in border regions is simultaneously a public health, economic, and national security failure.

source.quote: Youth drug prevalence in 15-35 age group was 38 per cent in border districts.

recommendations: Ensure uninterrupted buprenorphine supply to all 600 OAT clinics through a 3-month buffer stock policy and state-level emergency procurement authority -- a single medicine shortage must not break a patient's recovery.
Scale OAT treatment coverage from 28% to 60% within 3 years by opening 300 additional OOAT centres in border districts and residential colonies with highest prevalence.

Improve prosecution quality by assigning dedicated special public prosecutors to all drug cases with minimum 5-year experience; the 18% conviction rate is a legal system failure, not an evidence shortage.
Spend all ₹280 crore drug fund proceeds on border-district youth prevention programmes, school counselling, and community de-addiction camps within 2 years.

title: Performance Audit on Samagra Shiksha -- Government of Assam
ministry: Education Department, Government of Assam
overview: CAG audited Samagra Shiksha in Assam -- a state with 1.12 crore school-enrolled children and persistent learning deficits. Despite ₹8,420 crore spent over five years, Class V reading proficiency was 42% and numeracy was 38% -- among the lowest in India. 28% of schools had single-teacher classrooms across multiple grades. Teacher vacancies were 32% in upper primary schools. ₹1,820 crore in civil works (classrooms, toilets, boundary walls) were incomplete after 3+ years. Dropout rate in Classes IX-X was 22% -- the highest for any state with a Samagra Shiksha allocation above ₹5,000 crore. Midday meal programme coverage was 88% but nutritional quality testing was done in only 28% of schools.

stats.label: Class V reading proficiency
stats.note: Among the lowest large-state reading outcomes; 58% of Assam's primary children cannot read at grade level after 5 years of schooling

source.quote: Class V reading proficiency was 42 per cent -- among the lowest in India.

stats.label: Upper primary teacher vacancy
stats.note: One in three upper primary teaching posts unfilled; single-teacher schools managing multiple grades cover 28% of school stock

source.quote: Teacher vacancies were 32 per cent in upper primary schools.
